questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an amorphous solid?
questions.explanation: Glass has only short-range order and no sharp melting point, so it is amorphous; the others are crystalline.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many atoms effectively belong to one face-centred cubic (fcc) unit cell?
questions.explanation: 8 corners x 1/8 + 6 face centres x 1/2 = 1 + 3 = 4 atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the packing efficiency of a body-centred cubic (bcc) structure?
questions.explanation: Simple cubic is 52.4%, bcc is about 68% and fcc/hcp are 74%.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which defect lowers the density of an ionic crystal because equal numbers of cations and anions are missing from the lattice?
options: Interstitial defect in a metal crystal
questions.explanation: In a Schottky defect, pairs of oppositely charged ions leave the crystal, so the density decreases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Copper crystallises in an fcc lattice with edge length 361 pm. Taking the molar mass of Cu as 63.5 g/mol and N_A = 6.022 x 10²³ mol⁻¹, its density is closest to:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In an ionic solid the radius ratio r(cation)/r(anion) is 0.50. The cation is most likely surrounded by how many anions?
questions.explanation: A radius ratio of 0.414–0.732 corresponds to an octahedral void, giving coordination number 6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State two differences between crystalline and amorphous solids.
questions.answer: Crystalline solids have long-range regular arrangement of particles, a sharp melting point and are anisotropic; amorphous solids have only short-range order, melt over a range of temperature and are isotropic.
keyPoints: Crystalline: long-range order; amorphous: short-range order
Crystalline: sharp melting point; amorphous: melts over a range
Crystalline are anisotropic; amorphous are isotropic
questions.explanation: The order in the arrangement of particles decides the melting behaviour and the directional properties.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many unit cells are present in 1 mole of a metal that crystallises in an fcc structure?
questions.explanation: Each fcc cell has 4 atoms, so the number of cells is one quarter of Avogadro's number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Molality is defined as the number of moles of solute per:
questions.explanation: Molality (m) = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg; it does not change with temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which statement is Henry's law?
options: The vapour pressure of a solution is proportional to the mole fraction of the solvent.
The partial pressure of a gas over a solution is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.
The elevation in boiling point is proportional to the molality of the solute.
The osmotic pressure of a solution depends only on temperature.
questions.explanation: Henry's law: p = K_H x, where x is the mole fraction of the dissolved gas.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the van't Hoff factor for a dilute solution of K₂SO₄ if it dissociates completely?
questions.explanation: K₂SO₄ gives 2 K⁺ and 1 SO₄²⁻, i.e. 3 particles per formula unit, so i = 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 18 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol) is dissolved in 500 g of water. The molality of the solution is:
questions.explanation: Moles = 18/180 = 0.1; mass of solvent = 0.5 kg; molality = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 m.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 6.0 g of urea (molar mass 60 g/mol) is dissolved in 200 g of water. Taking K_f of water as 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹, the depression in freezing point is:
questions.explanation: Moles of urea = 0.1; molality = 0.1/0.2 = 0.5 m; ΔT_f = 1.86 x 0.5 = 0.93 K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A mixture of acetone and chloroform shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. This is because:
options: acetone–chloroform attractions are weaker than those in the pure liquids
hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform makes the A–B attractions stronger than A–A and B–B
questions.explanation: Stronger A–B interactions lower the vapour pressure below the ideal value; mixing is exothermic with a decrease in volume.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components.
questions.answer: For a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution: p₁ = x₁p₁°, and the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressures.
keyPoints: Partial vapour pressure of a component is proportional to its mole fraction
p = x p° (p° is the vapour pressure of the pure component)
Total pressure = sum of partial pressures
questions.explanation: Raoult's law holds for ideal solutions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The molar mass of acetic acid determined from the freezing point depression in benzene is nearly double its actual value. Explain.
questions.answer: In benzene, acetic acid molecules associate into dimers through hydrogen bonding, so the number of particles is about half. The van't Hoff factor is about 0.5, and since molar mass is inversely proportional to the colligative effect, the observed molar mass is about double.
keyPoints: Acetic acid dimerises in benzene via hydrogen bonds
Number of solute particles decreases, so i ≈ 0.5
Observed colligative effect is smaller, so calculated molar mass is larger (about twice)
questions.explanation: Association reduces the number of particles and so the measured colligative property.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At which electrode does oxidation take place in a galvanic cell?
questions.explanation: Oxidation (loss of electrons) always occurs at the anode.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the SI unit of molar conductivity?
questions.explanation: Λm = κ/c, so the unit is S m⁻¹ / (mol m⁻³) = S m² mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Given E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, what is the standard EMF of the Daniell cell Zn | Zn²⁺ || Cu²⁺ | Cu?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How much charge is required to deposit 1 mole of aluminium from Al³⁺ ions? (F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al needs 3 F = 3 x 96 500 = 2.895 x 10⁵ C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A current of 2.0 A is passed through aqueous CuSO₄ for 1930 s using copper electrodes. Taking the molar mass of Cu as 63.5 g/mol and F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹, the mass of copper deposited is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Standard electrode potentials are: Zn²⁺/Zn −0.76 V, Fe²⁺/Fe −0.44 V, Cu²⁺/Cu +0.34 V, Mg²⁺/Mg −2.37 V. Which metal will not liberate hydrogen from dilute HCl?
questions.explanation: Only metals with negative E° (more reducing than H₂, E° = 0) displace hydrogen; copper has E° = +0.34 V.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions.
questions.answer: At infinite dilution, the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the limiting molar conductivities of its cations and anions, each ion contributing independently of the other ion present.
keyPoints: Each ion contributes a fixed value independent of the other ion
questions.explanation: The law is used to find Λm° of weak electrolytes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the EMF at 298 K of the cell Zn | Zn²⁺(0.01 M) || Cu²⁺(1 M) | Cu, given E°cell = 1.10 V. Use 2.303RT/F = 0.0592 V.
questions.explanation: A lower product concentration makes the cell EMF larger than E°.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the unit of the rate constant of a first-order reaction?
questions.explanation: For rate = k[A], k = rate/[A] = (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹)/(mol L⁻¹) = s⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The molecularity of an elementary reaction can be:
options: a positive whole number such as 1, 2 or 3
questions.explanation: Molecularity is the number of species colliding in an elementary step, so it is a whole number (rarely above 3).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0693 min⁻¹. What is its half-life?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The rate of a reaction usually increases with temperature mainly because:
options: the fraction of molecules with energy equal to or above the activation energy increases
the enthalpy of reaction becomes more negative
questions.explanation: According to the Arrhenius equation and the Maxwell distribution, more molecules cross the energy barrier at higher temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 30 minutes. Its half-life is:
questions.explanation: 75% completion equals two half-lives (100 → 50 → 25% left), so t½ = 30/2 = 15 min.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For a reaction with rate = k[A]²[B], the concentration of A is doubled and that of B is halved. The rate becomes:
questions.explanation: New rate = k(2[A])²(½[B]) = 4 x ½ = 2 times the original.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write two differences between the order and the molecularity of a reaction.
questions.answer: Order is determined experimentally from the rate law and can be zero, fractional or a whole number; molecularity is theoretical, applies to an elementary step and is always a positive whole number. Order applies to the overall reaction, molecularity to elementary steps.
keyPoints: Order is experimental; molecularity is theoretical
Order can be zero or fractional; molecularity cannot
Molecularity refers to elementary steps only
questions.explanation: A complex reaction has an order but its molecularity is defined only for each step.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction is 20% complete in 10 minutes. Calculate its rate constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Adsorption is best described as:
options: accumulation of a substance on the surface of another substance
uniform distribution of a substance throughout the bulk of a solid
dissolution of a gas in the interior of a liquid only
release of a gas from the surface of a solid
questions.explanation: Adsorption is a surface phenomenon; uniform uptake throughout the bulk is absorption.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Physisorption is caused by:
questions.explanation: Physical adsorption involves weak van der Waals forces, unlike chemisorption which involves chemical bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The Tyndall effect shown by colloidal solutions is due to:
options: absorption of light by the particles
scattering of light by the colloidal particles
reflection of light from the walls of the container
questions.explanation: Colloidal particles are large enough to scatter light, making the path of a beam visible.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following forms a lyophilic colloid with water?
questions.explanation: Starch forms a stable, reversible, solvent-loving (lyophilic) sol; metal and metal-sulphide sols are lyophobic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which ion is the most effective in coagulating a negatively charged arsenious sulphide sol?
questions.explanation: By the Hardy–Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an oppositely charged ion increases with its charge; Al³⁺ has the highest charge.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by:
options: providing an alternative path with lower activation energy without changing ΔH
raising the temperature of the system
shifting the equilibrium towards the products
changing the enthalpy of the reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers E_a for both forward and reverse reactions equally and leaves ΔH and the equilibrium position unchanged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Give two differences between physisorption and chemisorption.
questions.answer: Physisorption involves weak van der Waals forces, is reversible, has low enthalpy of adsorption (about 20–40 kJ/mol) and decreases as temperature rises; chemisorption involves chemical bonds, is irreversible, has high enthalpy (80–240 kJ/mol) and is highly specific.
keyPoints: Physisorption: van der Waals forces; chemisorption: chemical bonds
Physisorption is reversible and non-specific; chemisorption is irreversible and specific
Enthalpy of adsorption is low for physisorption and high for chemisorption
questions.explanation: The nature of the force decides the strength and reversibility of adsorption.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is ammonia adsorbed on charcoal much more than hydrogen?
questions.answer: Ammonia is more easily liquefiable and has a higher critical temperature, so it has stronger van der Waals forces and is adsorbed to a greater extent than hydrogen.
keyPoints: Easily liquefiable gases have higher critical temperatures
Stronger van der Waals forces with the adsorbent
Hydrogen has very weak intermolecular forces
questions.explanation: Extent of physisorption increases with the ease of liquefaction of the gas.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Bartlett prepared the first noble gas compound using which element?
questions.explanation: Xenon reacted with PtF₆ to give the first noble gas compound, XePtF₆.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which halogen has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases down group 17, so fluorine is the most electronegative element of all.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of the ammonia molecule?
questions.explanation: NH₃ has three bond pairs and one lone pair on nitrogen (sp³), giving a pyramidal shape.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The Ostwald process is used for the industrial manufacture of:
questions.explanation: Ostwald process: catalytic oxidation of ammonia to NO, then to NO₂, which is absorbed in water to give HNO₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of phosphorus in H₃PO₃?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Water is a liquid at room temperature while H₂S is a gas mainly because:
options: H₂O has a higher molar mass than H₂S
sulphur is more electronegative than oxygen
H₂S forms stronger hydrogen bonds than H₂O
H₂O molecules are associated through hydrogen bonds
questions.explanation: Oxygen is small and highly electronegative, so water molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, raising the boiling point.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is dinitrogen very unreactive at room temperature?
questions.answer: The two nitrogen atoms are joined by a triple bond (N≡N) with a very high bond dissociation enthalpy (about 941 kJ/mol), so a large amount of energy is needed to break it and N₂ is inert under ordinary conditions.
questions.explanation: Strong bonding and a non-polar molecule make N₂ chemically inert at room temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does phosphorus form PCl₅ but nitrogen does not form NCl₅?
questions.answer: Phosphorus has vacant 3d orbitals and can expand its octet to show covalency 5; nitrogen has no d orbitals in its second shell and cannot exceed a covalency of four.
keyPoints: N has no d orbitals in its valence shell
questions.explanation: Availability of d orbitals allows expansion of the octet for P but not for N.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The most common oxidation state shown by the lanthanoids is:
questions.explanation: All lanthanoids show +3; +2 and +4 occur only in a few cases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The colour of an aqueous solution of potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) is:
questions.explanation: The MnO₄⁻ ion is intensely purple.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Zinc (3d¹⁰4s²) is usually not regarded as a transition element because:
options: it has only one oxidation state in its atom
both the atom and its common ion (Zn²⁺) have a completely filled d subshell
questions.explanation: A transition element should have an incomplete d subshell in the atom or in a common ion; Zn has 3d¹⁰ in both.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Lanthanoid contraction is mainly due to:
options: the increase in the number of shells along the series
poor shielding of the nuclear charge by 4f electrons
decrease in nuclear charge along the series
questions.explanation: 4f electrons shield poorly, so increasing nuclear charge pulls the outer electrons in and radii decrease steadily.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of manganese in K₂MnO₄?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which ion is expected to be colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Sc³⁺ has a 3d⁰ configuration, so no d–d transition is possible; the other ions have partly filled d orbitals.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write any three characteristic properties of transition elements.
questions.answer: They show variable oxidation states, form coloured compounds, form complex compounds, show catalytic activity, and many of their ions are paramagnetic.
keyPoints: Formation of coloured ions and complexes
questions.explanation: These arise from the partly filled d orbitals.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (atomic number of Mn = 25).
questions.answer: Mn²⁺ is 3d⁵, with n = 5 unpaired electrons. μ = √[n(n+2)] = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM.
questions.explanation: Spin-only formula: μ = √[n(n+2)] Bohr magnetons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of cobalt in [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃?
questions.explanation: Six NH₃ ligands are directly bonded to Co³⁺ inside the coordination sphere.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a bidentate ligand?
questions.explanation: Ethane-1,2-diamine has two nitrogen donor atoms and binds through both.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of iron in K₄[Fe(CN)₆]?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of K₃[Fe(CN)₆] is:
questions.explanation: The complex ion [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ has Fe in +3 state, hence ferrate(III).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ (Ni²⁺ is d⁸, CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand) is:
questions.explanation: The strong field pairs the d electrons, giving dsp² hybridisation, a square planar shape and no unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ and [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br are examples of which type of isomerism?
questions.explanation: The two compounds give different ions in solution (SO₄²⁻ and Br⁻ respectively), which is ionisation isomerism.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define the terms 'ligand' and 'coordination number' with one example of each.
questions.answer: A ligand is an ion or molecule bound to the central metal atom/ion by a coordinate bond (e.g. NH₃, Cl⁻). The coordination number is the number of ligand donor atoms directly attached to the central metal (e.g. 6 in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺).
keyPoints: Ligand: donor ion or molecule attached to the metal
Coordination number: number of donor atoms bonded to the metal
questions.explanation: These are basic terms in Werner's theory.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ is an inner orbital, low-spin complex with one unpaired electron.
questions.answer: Fe³⁺ is d⁵. CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand, so the five d electrons pair up in the t₂g orbitals, leaving one unpaired electron. Two 3d orbitals become available, so d²sp³ hybridisation (inner orbital) occurs, giving an octahedral low-spin complex.
keyPoints: Fe³⁺ is d⁵ and CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand
Electrons pair up, leaving one unpaired electron
questions.explanation: Strong-field ligands force pairing, giving a low-spin inner orbital complex.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂Br?
questions.explanation: A three-carbon chain with bromine on the end carbon is 1-bromopropane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An alkyl halide reacts with aqueous KOH mainly to give:
questions.explanation: Aqueous KOH brings about nucleophilic substitution of the halogen by OH⁻, giving an alcohol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reacts fastest by the S_N1 mechanism?
questions.explanation: Tertiary halides give the most stable carbocation, so they react fastest by S_N1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride on treatment with Cu₂Cl₂/HCl gives:
questions.explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction, which replaces the diazonium group by chlorine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Chlorobenzene is much less reactive than ethyl chloride towards nucleophilic substitution mainly because:
options: the C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene is longer than in ethyl chloride
resonance gives the C–Cl bond partial double bond character and the carbon is sp² hybridised
chlorine is not electronegative in aryl halides
questions.explanation: Delocalisation of chlorine's lone pair into the ring and the sp² carbon make the C–Cl bond shorter and stronger, so it is hard to break.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is optically active?
questions.explanation: In 2-bromobutane, C-2 is bonded to four different groups (H, Br, CH₃, C₂H₅), so it is chiral.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the Finkelstein reaction? Give an example.
questions.answer: Alkyl chlorides or bromides are heated with NaI in dry acetone to form alkyl iodides, e.g. CH₃CH₂Br + NaI → CH₃CH₂I + NaBr. NaBr or NaCl precipitates in acetone, driving the reaction forward.
keyPoints: NaCl/NaBr is insoluble in acetone and precipitates
questions.explanation: It is a halogen exchange reaction by S_N2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is the dipole moment of chlorobenzene lower than that of cyclohexyl chloride?
questions.answer: In chlorobenzene the C–Cl carbon is sp² hybridised and more electronegative than an sp³ carbon, and resonance partly shifts chlorine's electron density into the ring. Both effects reduce the charge separation, so the dipole moment is lower.
keyPoints: sp² carbon is more electronegative than sp³ carbon
Resonance reduces the negative charge on chlorine
Smaller charge separation gives a lower dipole moment
questions.explanation: Hybridisation and resonance both lower the polarity of the C–Cl bond in chlorobenzene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In phenol, the –OH group is attached to:
options: an sp³ carbon of an alkyl chain
a carbon atom of a benzene ring
questions.explanation: Phenols have the –OH group bonded directly to an sp² carbon of an aromatic ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which enzyme converts glucose into ethanol during fermentation?
questions.explanation: Zymase in yeast converts glucose and fructose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which alcohol gives turbidity immediately with Lucas reagent at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols form the most stable carbocation and react at once with HCl/ZnCl₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give:
questions.explanation: The –OH group strongly activates the ring, giving a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol mainly because:
options: the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance
phenol has a higher molar mass
ethoxide ion is stabilised by resonance
questions.explanation: The negative charge of the phenoxide ion is delocalised into the benzene ring, which stabilises it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of reactants is best for preparing methyl tert-butyl ether, CH₃–O–C(CH₃)₃, by Williamson synthesis?
questions.explanation: The alkyl halide must be primary; a tertiary halide would give an alkene by elimination.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Name the reaction in which phenol is converted to salicylaldehyde and state the reagents used.
questions.answer: It is the Reimer–Tiemann reaction. Phenol is treated with chloroform and aqueous sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification, to give salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde).
keyPoints: CHCl₃ and aqueous NaOH, then acid
questions.explanation: Dichlorocarbene attacks the ortho position of the phenoxide ion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why ethanol has a much higher boiling point than methoxymethane although both have the same molecular formula.
questions.answer: Ethanol molecules form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through the O–H group, so more energy is needed to separate them. Methoxymethane has no O–H bond, cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself, and has only weaker dipole–dipole forces.
keyPoints: Ethanol has an O–H group and shows intermolecular hydrogen bonding
Methoxymethane has no O–H and cannot hydrogen-bond with itself
Hydrogen bonds need more energy to break
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding raises the boiling point of alcohols.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the functional group of an aldehyde?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes contain the –CHO group; ketones have a C=O between two carbon atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent gives a silver mirror with aldehydes?
questions.explanation: Ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent) is reduced to silver by aldehydes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following does not undergo aldol condensation?
questions.explanation: Methanal has no α-hydrogen atoms, which are necessary for aldol condensation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanal on reduction with NaBH₄ gives:
questions.explanation: NaBH₄ reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH. The products are:
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (disproportionation) to give the alcohol and the carboxylate salt.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: Three electron-withdrawing chlorine atoms stabilise the carboxylate ion most through the –I effect.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is Rosenmund reduction? Give an example.
questions.answer: It is the partial reduction of an acyl chloride to an aldehyde by hydrogen over palladium on barium sulphate (a poisoned catalyst), e.g. CH₃COCl + H₂ → CH₃CHO + HCl.
keyPoints: Example such as CH₃COCl to CH₃CHO
questions.explanation: The poisoned catalyst stops the reduction at the aldehyde stage.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why are carboxylic acids more acidic than phenols?
questions.answer: The carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance with two equivalent structures that share the negative charge over two electronegative oxygen atoms. In the phenoxide ion the charge is partly delocalised onto less electronegative carbon atoms, so it is less stable.
keyPoints: Carboxylate has two equivalent resonance structures
Charge is shared by two electronegative oxygen atoms
Phenoxide charge is delocalised onto carbon, giving less stabilisation
questions.explanation: A more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: CH₃–NH–CH₃ is a:
questions.explanation: The nitrogen is bonded to two alkyl groups and one hydrogen, so it is a secondary amine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent is known as Hinsberg's reagent?
questions.explanation: Benzenesulphonyl chloride is used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Nitrobenzene on reduction with Sn and concentrated HCl gives:
questions.explanation: The nitro group is reduced to an amino group, giving aniline.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the strongest base in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Alkyl groups increase electron density on nitrogen, so dimethylamine is more basic than ammonia, trimethylamine (solvation effect) or aniline (lone pair delocalised).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for preparing:
options: aromatic primary amines such as aniline
questions.explanation: Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with potassium phthalimide, so only aliphatic primary amines are formed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which compound gives a foul-smelling isocyanide on heating with chloroform and alcoholic KOH?
questions.explanation: Only primary amines give the carbylamine reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the diazotisation of aniline.
questions.answer: C₆H₅NH₂ + NaNO₂ + 2HCl → C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + NaCl + 2H₂O, carried out at 273–278 K (0–5 °C).
keyPoints: Aniline reacts with NaNO₂ and HCl
questions.explanation: Nitrous acid is generated in situ from NaNO₂ and HCl.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is aniline a weaker base than methylamine?
questions.answer: In aniline the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance, so it is less available to accept a proton. In methylamine the +I effect of the methyl group increases electron density on nitrogen.
keyPoints: Lone pair of aniline is delocalised into the ring
Methyl group has +I effect in methylamine
questions.explanation: Availability of the lone pair determines basic strength.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Glucose is classified as:
questions.explanation: Glucose has six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On hydrolysis sucrose gives:
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide of α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A peptide bond is formed between:
options: the –COOH group of one amino acid and the –NH₂ group of another
the side chains of two amino acids only
questions.explanation: Condensation of –COOH and –NH₂ with loss of water forms the –CO–NH– peptide (amide) linkage.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes scurvy, with bleeding gums.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: When egg white is boiled, the change is best described as:
options: hydrolysis of peptide bonds into amino acids
denaturation, with loss of higher-order structure but the primary structure intact
questions.explanation: Heat disrupts hydrogen bonds, destroying the secondary and tertiary structure; the amino acid sequence is unchanged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of components is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains the sugar ribose and the base uracil; DNA has deoxyribose and thymine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between essential and non-essential amino acids with one example of each.
questions.answer: Essential amino acids cannot be synthesised by the body and must be obtained from the diet (e.g. valine, leucine). Non-essential amino acids can be synthesised in the body (e.g. glycine, alanine).
keyPoints: Essential: not made in the body, supplied by food
questions.explanation: Whether the body can make the amino acid decides the classification.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is the hydrolysis product of sucrose called invert sugar?
questions.answer: Sucrose is dextrorotatory, but its hydrolysis gives an equimolar mixture of D-glucose (dextrorotatory) and D-fructose (more strongly laevorotatory). The mixture is laevorotatory, so the sign of rotation is inverted.
keyPoints: Fructose is more laevorotatory, so the mixture is laevorotatory (rotation inverted)
questions.explanation: The change of optical rotation from + to − is called inversion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a molecular solid?
questions.explanation: Solid CO₂ consists of discrete molecules held by weak van der Waals forces.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of an atom in hexagonal close packing (hcp) or cubic close packing (ccp)?
questions.explanation: Each sphere touches 6 in its own layer, 3 above and 3 below, giving 12.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Alkali halide crystals heated in the vapour of the alkali metal acquire colour. The colour is due to:
questions.explanation: Excess metal atoms create anion vacancies occupied by electrons, which absorb visible light.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In a close-packed lattice of N atoms, the numbers of octahedral and tetrahedral voids are respectively:
questions.explanation: There is one octahedral void and two tetrahedral voids per atom.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Atoms of element B form a ccp lattice and atoms of A occupy two-thirds of the octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is:
questions.explanation: For N atoms of B there are N octahedral voids, so A = 2N/3. A : B = 2/3 : 1 = 2 : 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A cubic crystal of an element has molar mass 52 g/mol, density 7.2 g cm⁻³ and edge 289 pm (N_A = 6.022 x 10²³). Its unit cell is:
questions.explanation: Z = dN_A a³/M = 7.2 x 6.022 x 10²³ x (2.89 x 10⁻⁸)³/52 ≈ 2.0, which is bcc.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is a Frenkel defect? Name one compound that shows it and give one effect on the crystal.
questions.answer: In a Frenkel defect a smaller ion (usually the cation) leaves its lattice site and occupies an interstitial site. It is shown by AgBr, AgCl or ZnS. The density of the crystal remains unchanged.
keyPoints: Smaller ion moves to an interstitial position
questions.explanation: No ions leave the crystal in a Frenkel defect, only change position.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A metal crystallises in an fcc lattice with edge length 400 pm. Calculate the radius of the metal atom.
questions.answer: In fcc, atoms touch along the face diagonal: 4r = √2 a, so r = a/(2√2) = 400/2.828 ≈ 141 pm.
questions.explanation: The face diagonal of the cube passes through three atoms in contact.

crossCheck.note: The 141 pm value is right, but keyPoint 2 has wrong algebra ("4r = √2 a / r"). The correct relation is 4r = √2 a, so r = a/(2√2). Reviewed: kept; the key is right.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a colligative property?
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend on the number of solute particles; depression of freezing point is one of them.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The sum of the mole fractions of all components in a solution is:
questions.explanation: Mole fractions are fractions of the total number of moles, so they add up to 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the osmotic pressure of a 0.01 mol/L solution of a non-electrolyte at 300 K? (R = 0.0821 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Two solutions are isotonic when they have the same:
options: osmotic pressure at the same temperature
questions.explanation: Isotonic solutions exert equal osmotic pressure at a given temperature, so there is no net flow across a semipermeable membrane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 10 g of a non-volatile solute (molar mass 100 g/mol) is dissolved in 250 g of water. Taking K_b of water as 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹, the elevation of boiling point is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Four aqueous solutions each of molality 0.1 m are listed. Assuming complete dissociation of electrolytes, which has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: CaCl₂ gives 3 particles (i = 3), more than NaCl (2) or the non-electrolytes (1), so it has the largest elevation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is an azeotrope?
questions.answer: An azeotrope is a liquid mixture that boils at a constant temperature and distils over with the same composition as the liquid, so its components cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
keyPoints: Liquid and vapour have the same composition; cannot be separated by fractional distillation
questions.explanation: Azeotropes arise from large deviations from Raoult's law.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the mole fraction of ethanol in a solution of 4.6 g ethanol (C₂H₅OH, 46 g/mol) in 36 g of water (18 g/mol).
questions.answer: Moles of ethanol = 4.6/46 = 0.1; moles of water = 36/18 = 2.0. Mole fraction of ethanol = 0.1/(0.1 + 2.0) = 0.1/2.1 ≈ 0.048.
questions.explanation: Mole fraction is moles of the component divided by total moles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the function of a salt bridge in a galvanic cell?
options: It completes the circuit and maintains electrical neutrality of the two solutions
It supplies electrons to the cathode
It increases the EMF of the cell
questions.explanation: Ions migrate through the salt bridge to balance the charge built up in the half-cells.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary cell?
questions.explanation: A lead storage battery can be recharged, so it is a secondary cell.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: During discharge of a lead storage battery, the density of the sulphuric acid electrolyte:
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ is consumed to form PbSO₄ and water is produced, so the solution becomes less dense.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: When a solution of a strong electrolyte is diluted, its molar conductivity:
questions.explanation: On dilution ions move more freely with less inter-ionic attraction, so Λm rises towards its limiting value.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Iron pipelines are protected by connecting them to blocks of magnesium because:
options: magnesium is less reactive than iron
magnesium forms a thick oxide layer on iron
magnesium is oxidised in preference to iron and acts as a sacrificial anode
magnesium makes the iron a cathode of an electrolytic cell
questions.explanation: Mg has a more negative electrode potential, so it corrodes instead of iron.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride (brine), the product liberated at the cathode is:
questions.explanation: Water is reduced more easily than Na⁺, so H₂ is formed at the cathode (and Cl₂ at the anode).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the electrode reactions and the overall reaction of the alkaline hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell.
keyPoints: Anode: hydrogen oxidised in presence of OH⁻
questions.explanation: The fuel cell converts chemical energy directly into electrical energy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The conductivity of a 0.1 mol/L KCl solution is 0.0129 S cm⁻¹. Calculate its molar conductivity.
keyPoints: Λm = κ x 1000 / c (c in mol L⁻¹)
Substitute κ = 0.0129 S cm⁻¹ and c = 0.1
questions.explanation: 1000/c converts the volume per mole into cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The rate law of a reaction is expressed in terms of:
options: the stoichiometric coefficients of the balanced equation only
the molecularity of the overall reaction
concentrations of reactants raised to powers determined experimentally
questions.explanation: The powers in the rate law (the orders) are found from experiment and need not equal the coefficients.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reaction whose rate does not depend on the concentration of the reactant has an order of:
questions.explanation: For a zero-order reaction, rate = k[A]⁰ = k, which is constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A plot of ln k against 1/T is a straight line whose slope is:
questions.explanation: ln k = ln A − E_a/(RT), so the slope is −E_a/R and the intercept is ln A.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For a zero-order reaction, the half-life is:
options: inversely proportional to the initial concentration
directly proportional to the initial concentration
proportional to the square of the initial concentration
questions.explanation: For zero order, t½ = [A]₀/2k, so it is proportional to [A]₀.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In a reaction the concentration of the reactant falls from 0.8 M to 0.4 M in 20 minutes and from 0.4 M to 0.2 M in the next 20 minutes. The order of the reaction is:
questions.explanation: A constant half-life (20 min) independent of concentration is the characteristic of a first-order reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A zero-order reaction has k = 0.01 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ and an initial concentration of 0.5 mol L⁻¹. The time taken for the reactant to be completely consumed is:
questions.explanation: For zero order, [A] = [A]₀ − kt, so t = 0.5/0.01 = 50 s.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are pseudo first-order reactions? Give an example.
questions.answer: A reaction that is actually of higher molecularity but behaves as first order because one reactant is present in large excess, so its concentration is practically constant. Example: acid-catalysed hydrolysis of ethyl acetate (excess water) or inversion of cane sugar.
keyPoints: One reactant is in large excess, its concentration is constant
Example such as hydrolysis of ester or inversion of sucrose
questions.explanation: The excess reactant's concentration is absorbed into the rate constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction has k = 2.303 x 10⁻² min⁻¹. How long does it take for 90% of the reactant to be consumed?
questions.explanation: Since 2.303/k = 100 min and log 10 = 1, the time is 100 min.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Smoke is a colloidal system of:
options: a gas dispersed in a liquid
a liquid dispersed in a gas
a solid dispersed in a gas
a solid dispersed in a liquid
questions.explanation: Smoke consists of fine solid particles dispersed in air; it is an aerosol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Milk is a colloidal system classified as:
questions.explanation: Milk has fat droplets dispersed in water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Brownian movement of colloidal particles is caused by:
options: the electric charge on the particles
bombardment of the particles by molecules of the dispersion medium
questions.explanation: Unbalanced collisions with the medium's molecules make the particles move in a zig-zag path, which also keeps the sol stable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of heterogeneous catalysis?
options: Hydrolysis of an ester with dilute HCl
Combination of N₂ and H₂ over iron in the Haber process
Oxidation of SO₂ with NO in the lead-chamber process
Decomposition of an ester in aqueous acid
questions.explanation: Here the catalyst (solid iron) is in a different phase from the gaseous reactants.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At very high pressure the extent of adsorption of a gas on a solid becomes independent of pressure. In the Freundlich equation x/m = kP^(1/n) this corresponds to 1/n being:
questions.explanation: When 1/n = 0, P⁰ = 1, so x/m = k and adsorption is constant (saturation).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst whose selectivity depends on the pore structure and on the size and shape of the reactant and product molecules is called a:
questions.explanation: Zeolites are shape-selective catalysts, because only molecules that fit the pores can react or leave.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is electrophoresis? What does it show about a colloidal sol?
questions.answer: Electrophoresis is the movement of colloidal particles towards one of the electrodes under an applied electric field. It shows that colloidal particles carry an electric charge.
keyPoints: Movement of colloidal particles in an electric field
Particles move towards the oppositely charged electrode
Proves that colloidal particles are charged
questions.explanation: The direction of migration shows the sign of the charge.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does the extent of physisorption of a gas decrease when the temperature is raised?
questions.answer: Adsorption is exothermic (ΔH is negative). By Le Chatelier's principle, raising the temperature favours the reverse process (desorption), and the weak van der Waals forces cannot hold the gas molecules at higher thermal energy.
keyPoints: Le Chatelier: higher temperature favours desorption
Weak van der Waals forces are overcome by thermal motion
questions.explanation: Physisorption is generally high at low temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which noble gas is used for filling weather balloons because it is light and non-inflammable?
questions.explanation: Helium is the second lightest gas and does not burn.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Bleaching powder is represented by the formula:
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over slaked lime and is represented as CaOCl₂ (Ca(OCl)Cl).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which catalyst is used in the Contact process for the manufacture of sulphuric acid?
questions.explanation: V₂O₅ catalyses the oxidation of SO₂ to SO₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of sulphur in SF₆?
questions.explanation: Six bond pairs and no lone pair give an octahedral shape with sp³d² hybridisation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among HClO, HClO₂, HClO₃ and HClO₄, the strongest acid is:
questions.explanation: More oxygen atoms disperse the negative charge of the anion better, so the acid strength increases with oxidation state of chlorine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The H–N–H bond angle in NH₃ (about 107°) is larger than the H–P–H angle in PH₃ (about 94°) because:
options: phosphorus is larger, so its lone pair is more spread out
nitrogen is more electronegative, so bond pairs lie nearer to N and repel more
PH₃ has no lone pair on phosphorus
questions.explanation: Bond pairs close to the central atom repel each other more strongly, widening the angle; in PH₃ they lie farther from P.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the industrial manufacture of ammonia by Haber's process and state the conditions.
questions.answer: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH = −92.4 kJ (that is, −46.1 kJ per mole of NH₃). Conditions: iron catalyst with promoters, about 200 atm pressure and about 700 K.
keyPoints: High pressure (about 200 atm) and about 700 K
questions.explanation: High pressure favours ammonia; moderate temperature balances yield and rate.

crossCheck.note: The ΔH value is misstated. -46.1 kJ/mol is per mole of NH3. For the equation as written (N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3) ΔH is about -92.4 kJ. The conditions are correct. Fixed after review: ΔH for the equation as written is −92.4 kJ (−46.1 kJ per mole of NH₃).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is HF a weak acid in water while HCl is a strong acid?
questions.answer: The H–F bond is very strong (high bond enthalpy), so HF ionises only slightly. HF molecules and F⁻ ions are also strongly hydrogen bonded, which limits ionisation, whereas the weaker H–Cl bond breaks easily.
keyPoints: H–F bond is much stronger than H–Cl
Hence HF ionises only to a small extent
questions.explanation: Acid strength of hydrogen halides increases from HF to HI.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Brass is an alloy of copper and:
questions.explanation: Brass is Cu + Zn; bronze is Cu + Sn.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The colour of an acidified solution of potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇) is:
questions.explanation: Dichromate ions are orange; chromate ions are yellow.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is:
questions.explanation: A half-filled d subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron shifts to give 3d⁵4s¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following 3d-series elements shows the highest oxidation state of +7?
questions.explanation: Manganese can use all its 3d and 4s electrons (3d⁵4s²), giving +7 as in KMnO₄.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In acidic medium, one mole of MnO₄⁻ oxidises how many moles of Fe²⁺?
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O accepts 5 electrons, and each Fe²⁺ gives 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which ion has the maximum number of unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: Fe³⁺ is d⁵ with 5 unpaired electrons; Fe²⁺ has 4, Co²⁺ has 3 and Cu²⁺ has 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are interstitial compounds? State two of their characteristics.
questions.answer: Interstitial compounds are formed when small atoms such as H, C or N occupy the interstitial voids in the metal lattice. They are generally very hard, have high melting points, are chemically inert and retain metallic conductivity.
keyPoints: Small atoms (H, C, N) trapped in the voids of the metal lattice
Very hard with high melting points
questions.explanation: Examples are TiC and Fe₃H.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidising agent while Cr²⁺ is a strong reducing agent.
questions.answer: Mn³⁺ (d⁴) readily gains an electron to form the stable half-filled d⁵ ion Mn²⁺. Cr²⁺ (d⁴) readily loses an electron to form Cr³⁺ (d³, t₂g³), which is very stable.
keyPoints: Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives stable t₂g³ configuration
Stability of the product drives oxidising or reducing behaviour
questions.explanation: Both ions are d⁴ but their products are particularly stable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In Werner's theory the secondary valence of a metal corresponds to its:
questions.explanation: Secondary valence is non-ionisable and equals the coordination number; primary valence is the oxidation state.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of copper in [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺?
questions.explanation: NH₃ is neutral, so the charge on the metal equals the charge of the complex ion, +2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The formula of tetraamminedichloridocobalt(III) chloride is:
questions.explanation: Co³⁺ with 4 NH₃ and 2 Cl⁻ gives a +1 complex cation, balanced by one chloride.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The denticity of the ligand EDTA⁴⁻ is:
questions.explanation: EDTA binds through two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms, so it is hexadentate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many geometrical isomers are possible for the square planar complex [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]?
questions.explanation: The two Cl ligands can be adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Excess AgNO₃ is added to a solution containing 1 mole of [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂. How many moles of AgCl precipitate?
questions.explanation: Only the two ionisable chloride ions outside the coordination sphere precipitate; the coordinated Cl⁻ does not.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the IUPAC names of (i) [Ni(CO)₄] and (ii) K₂[PtCl₄].
questions.explanation: Ligands are named first, then the metal with its oxidation state.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why aqueous solutions of Cu²⁺ complexes are coloured but those of Zn²⁺ are colourless.
questions.answer: Cu²⁺ (d⁹) has a partially filled d subshell, so d–d transitions by absorption of visible light are possible and a complementary colour is seen. Zn²⁺ (d¹⁰) has a completely filled d subshell, so no d–d transition can occur and it is colourless.
keyPoints: Cu²⁺ is d⁹ and has a vacancy in d orbitals
Zn²⁺ is d¹⁰, no d–d transition
questions.explanation: Colour in complexes arises from d–d electronic transitions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The common name of CHCl₃ is:
questions.explanation: CHCl₃ is trichloromethane, commonly called chloroform.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) released into the atmosphere mainly damage the:
questions.explanation: In the stratosphere CFCs release chlorine atoms that catalytically destroy ozone.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which alkyl bromide reacts fastest by the S_N2 mechanism?
questions.explanation: S_N2 is fastest at the least hindered carbon, i.e. methyl, followed by primary, secondary and tertiary.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Methyl bromide reacts with sodium metal in dry ether to give:
questions.explanation: Wurtz reaction: 2CH₃Br + 2Na → CH₃–CH₃ + 2NaBr.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 2-Bromobutane is heated with alcoholic KOH. According to Saytzeff's rule the major product is:
questions.explanation: Elimination gives the more substituted, more stable alkene, but-2-ene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A racemic mixture is optically inactive because:
options: its molecules have a plane of symmetry
the equal and opposite rotations of the two enantiomers cancel each other
the enantiomers combine to form a meso compound
questions.explanation: A racemate has equal amounts of d and l forms, so net rotation is zero (external compensation).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is meant by an ambident nucleophile? Give one example.
questions.answer: An ambident nucleophile can attack through either of two different atoms, for example the cyanide ion (through C or N) or the nitrite ion (through N or O).
keyPoints: Nucleophile with two possible attacking sites
Gives two different products depending on the site
questions.explanation: The site of attack depends on the reaction conditions and the reagent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An alkyl halide gives an alkyl cyanide with KCN but an isocyanide with AgCN. Explain.
questions.answer: KCN is ionic and gives free CN⁻ ions, which attack through carbon (forming the stronger C–C bond) to give R–CN. AgCN is covalent, so only the nitrogen lone pair is available for attack, giving R–NC.
keyPoints: KCN is ionic: attack through carbon gives R–CN
AgCN is covalent: attack through nitrogen gives R–NC
questions.explanation: The nature of the cyanide salt decides which atom acts as the nucleophile.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Methanol is also known as:
questions.explanation: Methanol was originally obtained by destructive distillation of wood.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Commercial ethanol is denatured mainly to:
questions.explanation: Poisonous or foul-tasting substances (methanol, pyridine) are added so it cannot be misused as a beverage.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Acid-catalysed hydration of propene gives mainly:
questions.explanation: Water adds according to Markovnikov's rule, so –OH goes to the middle carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A primary alcohol can be oxidised to the aldehyde without going further to the acid by using:
questions.explanation: PCC is a mild oxidising agent that stops at the aldehyde stage.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.explanation: The –NO₂ group withdraws electrons and stabilises the phenoxide ion, whereas the –CH₃ group in p-cresol destabilises it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Anisole on heating with concentrated HI gives:
questions.explanation: The O–CH₃ bond cleaves because the C(aryl)–O bond is strong (partial double bond character) and does not break.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the dehydration of ethanol to ethene and state the conditions.
questions.answer: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O, on heating with concentrated H₂SO₄ at about 443 K.
keyPoints: Temperature about 443 K (at 413 K ether forms instead)
questions.explanation: Intramolecular dehydration occurs at the higher temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is o-nitrophenol more acidic than o-methoxyphenol?
questions.answer: The –NO₂ group is electron-withdrawing; it disperses the negative charge of the phenoxide ion and stabilises it. The –OCH₃ group is electron-releasing and intensifies the negative charge, destabilising the phenoxide ion.
keyPoints: –NO₂ withdraws electrons and stabilises the phenoxide ion
A more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid
questions.explanation: Substituents affect acidity through their influence on phenoxide stability.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CHO?
questions.explanation: A two-carbon aldehyde is ethanal (acetaldehyde).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of acetone is:
questions.explanation: Acetone, CH₃COCH₃, is propanone.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following does not reduce Fehling's solution?
questions.explanation: Aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde do not reduce Fehling's solution; aliphatic aldehydes do.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which compound gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform when warmed with I₂ and NaOH?
questions.explanation: Compounds containing a CH₃CO– group (methyl ketones) give the iodoform reaction; propanone has this group.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanoic acid heated with Cl₂ in the presence of red phosphorus (Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction) gives:
questions.explanation: The α-hydrogen is replaced by chlorine, giving ClCH₂COOH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Sodium ethanoate is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO). The main product is:
questions.explanation: Decarboxylation removes CO₂: CH₃COONa + NaOH → CH₄ + Na₂CO₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the Etard reaction?
questions.answer: Toluene is oxidised with chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) in CS₂ to form a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde.
questions.explanation: The reaction stops at the aldehyde and does not give benzoic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why are aldehydes more reactive than ketones towards nucleophilic addition?
questions.answer: In aldehydes the carbonyl carbon is attached to one alkyl group and one hydrogen, so there is less steric hindrance and less electron-donating (+I) effect, making the carbon more electrophilic. In ketones two bulky alkyl groups hinder attack and reduce the positive charge on carbon.
keyPoints: Only one electron-donating alkyl group, so carbonyl carbon is more positive
questions.explanation: Steric and electronic effects both favour aldehydes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aniline is an example of:
questions.explanation: Its –NH₂ group is attached directly to a benzene ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aqueous solutions of aliphatic amines are:
questions.explanation: Amines accept protons from water, producing OH⁻ ions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanamide (CH₃CONH₂) is treated with Br₂ and aqueous NaOH (Hofmann bromamide reaction). The product is:
questions.explanation: The amine formed has one carbon atom less than the amide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aniline reacts with bromine water to give:
questions.explanation: The –NH₂ group strongly activates the ring, giving a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is evolved when ethylamine reacts with nitrous acid (NaNO₂ + HCl)?
questions.explanation: Aliphatic primary amines give unstable diazonium salts that decompose to the alcohol and nitrogen gas.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In Hinsberg's test, which type of amine gives a sulphonamide that is insoluble in aqueous alkali?
questions.explanation: The sulphonamide of a secondary amine has no acidic N–H hydrogen, so it stays insoluble; that of a primary amine dissolves in alkali.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the reaction of ethylamine with ethanoyl chloride.
questions.answer: C₂H₅NH₂ + CH₃COCl → CH₃CONHC₂H₅ + HCl, forming N-ethylethanamide. A base such as pyridine removes the HCl.
keyPoints: HCl is formed and removed by a base
questions.explanation: Primary and secondary amines undergo acylation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is aniline not nitrated directly with a nitrating mixture to give mainly the para product?
questions.answer: In the strongly acidic mixture aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, which is meta-directing, giving a large amount of meta-nitroaniline. Aniline is also oxidised by nitric acid, forming tarry products.
keyPoints: Aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion
Oxidation by nitric acid causes tar
questions.explanation: Protecting the amino group by acetylation avoids these problems.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: In sucrose the reducing groups of glucose and fructose are tied up in the glycosidic bond, so it does not reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The main storage polysaccharide in plants is:
questions.explanation: Plants store glucose as starch; animals store it as glycogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Enzymes are mostly:
questions.explanation: Enzymes are globular proteins that act as biological catalysts.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many chiral carbon atoms are present in the open-chain structure of glucose?
questions.explanation: Carbons 2, 3, 4 and 5 each carry four different groups.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: α-D-Glucose and β-D-glucose are anomers that differ in the configuration at carbon number:
questions.explanation: Anomers differ at the new chiral centre (C-1) created on ring closure of the aldehyde group.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many hydrogen bonds join a guanine–cytosine base pair in DNA?
questions.explanation: G–C pairs have three hydrogen bonds, while A–T pairs have two.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are vitamins? Name the two broad groups with one example of each.
questions.answer: Vitamins are organic compounds required in small amounts for normal growth and health that the body cannot make in sufficient quantity. They are fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) or water-soluble (B group, C).
keyPoints: Organic compounds needed in small amounts
questions.explanation: Solubility determines whether a vitamin is stored in the body.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Amino acids have high melting points and are soluble in water but insoluble in non-polar solvents. Explain.
questions.answer: In the solid and in neutral solution an amino acid exists as a zwitterion (dipolar ion), H₃N⁺–CHR–COO⁻. The strong ionic attractions give high melting points, and the ionic character makes them soluble in polar water but not in non-polar solvents.
keyPoints: Strong electrostatic forces give high melting points
Ionic nature gives solubility in water, not in non-polar solvents
questions.explanation: The proton moves from the –COOH group to the –NH₂ group, forming a dipolar ion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which type of solid conducts electricity in the solid state through free electrons?
options: Covalent network solids such as diamond
questions.explanation: Metals have a sea of delocalised electrons that carries current even in the solid state.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many atoms effectively belong to one body-centred cubic unit cell?
questions.explanation: 8 corners x 1/8 + 1 body-centre atom = 2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Silicon doped with a small amount of phosphorus becomes a:
options: metallic conductor with no band gap
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has five valence electrons, so each dopant atom supplies one extra electron; this is n-type doping.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a ferromagnetic substance?
questions.explanation: Iron, cobalt and nickel are ferromagnetic; the others are diamagnetic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aluminium (molar mass 27 g/mol, density 2.7 g cm⁻³) crystallises in an fcc lattice. Taking N_A = 6.022 x 10²³, the edge length of its unit cell is about:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the rock-salt (NaCl) structure the Cl⁻ ions form a ccp lattice. The Na⁺ ions occupy:
questions.explanation: There are 4 Cl⁻ and 4 octahedral voids per unit cell, all filled by Na⁺, giving 1 : 1 stoichiometry and coordination number 6 : 6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between paramagnetic and diamagnetic substances.
questions.answer: Paramagnetic substances contain unpaired electrons and are weakly attracted by a magnetic field (e.g. O₂, Cu²⁺). Diamagnetic substances have all electrons paired and are weakly repelled by a magnetic field (e.g. H₂O, NaCl).
keyPoints: Diamagnetic: all electrons paired, weakly repelled
questions.explanation: Magnetic behaviour depends on the electron pairing.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the number of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions per unit cell of sodium chloride, which has Cl⁻ at the corners and face centres and Na⁺ at the edge centres and body centre.
questions.answer: Cl⁻: 8 x 1/8 + 6 x 1/2 = 4. Na⁺: 12 x 1/4 + 1 = 4. So each unit cell has 4 Na⁺ and 4 Cl⁻ ions, i.e. 4 formula units of NaCl.
questions.explanation: Corner atoms are shared by 8 cells, face atoms by 2 and edge atoms by 4.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An ideal solution is one that:
options: obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration
has a positive enthalpy of mixing
shows an increase in volume on mixing
questions.explanation: In an ideal solution ΔH_mix = 0 and ΔV_mix = 0, and Raoult's law holds at all concentrations.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The spontaneous flow of solvent through a semipermeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated one is called:
questions.explanation: This is osmosis; it continues until the osmotic pressure balances the flow.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reverse osmosis is used in:
options: converting a dilute solution into a concentrated one by evaporation
separating two miscible liquids by distillation
measuring the molar mass of gases
questions.explanation: A pressure greater than the osmotic pressure applied on the salt-water side forces water through the membrane, leaving the salt behind.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A 2.0 kg sample of water contains 10 mg of a dissolved salt. Its concentration in ppm by mass is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The Henry's law constant of a gas in water (mole-fraction form, p = K_H x) is 4 x 10⁴ atm at 298 K. If the partial pressure of the gas over water is 2 atm, its mole fraction in solution is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A 0.1 m aqueous solution of CaCl₂ is 50% dissociated. Taking K_f of water as 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹, the depression in freezing point is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State two characteristics of an ideal solution.
questions.answer: An ideal solution obeys Raoult's law at all concentrations; the enthalpy of mixing is zero (ΔH_mix = 0) and the volume change on mixing is zero (ΔV_mix = 0). The A–B interactions are similar in strength to the A–A and B–B interactions.
keyPoints: Obeys Raoult's law at all concentrations
questions.explanation: Mixtures such as n-hexane and n-heptane are nearly ideal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do aquatic animals feel more comfortable in cold water than in warm water?
questions.answer: The solubility of gases in liquids decreases with a rise in temperature (dissolution is exothermic). Cold water holds more dissolved oxygen, so aquatic life gets enough oxygen.
keyPoints: Solubility of gases decreases as temperature rises
Cold water has more dissolved oxygen
Warm water may not supply enough oxygen
questions.explanation: Gas dissolution is exothermic, so by Le Chatelier's principle it is favoured at lower temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The SI unit of resistivity is:
questions.explanation: ρ = R A / l, so its unit is ohm x metre.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is liberated at the anode during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: Cl⁻ ions are oxidised at the anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: By convention, the standard electrode potential of the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) is:
questions.explanation: SHE is taken as the reference, and its potential is defined as zero at all temperatures.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For the Daniell cell (E°cell = 1.10 V, n = 2), ΔG° is (F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹):

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For the Daniell cell with E°cell = 1.10 V at 298 K, log K_c for the cell reaction is (use 2.303RT/F = 0.0592 V):

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Given E° values: Li⁺/Li −3.05 V, Na⁺/Na −2.71 V, Zn²⁺/Zn −0.76 V, Cu²⁺/Cu +0.34 V. Which metal is the strongest reducing agent?
questions.explanation: The most negative E° belongs to the species most easily oxidised, i.e. lithium.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write two differences between a galvanic cell and an electrolytic cell.
questions.answer: A galvanic cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy through a spontaneous redox reaction; an electrolytic cell uses electrical energy to drive a non-spontaneous reaction. In a galvanic cell the anode is negative and the cathode positive; in an electrolytic cell the anode is positive and the cathode negative.
keyPoints: Galvanic: spontaneous reaction produces electricity; electrolytic: electricity drives a non-spontaneous reaction
Galvanic: anode −, cathode +; electrolytic: anode +, cathode −
questions.explanation: The direction of energy conversion and the polarity of the electrodes differ.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A current of 0.5 A is passed for 1930 s through a solution of silver nitrate. Calculate the mass of silver deposited (Ag = 108 g/mol, F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹).
questions.explanation: One mole of electrons deposits one mole of silver.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The rate constant of a reaction at a given temperature does not depend on:
questions.explanation: k depends on temperature, activation energy and catalyst, but not on the concentrations.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The activation energy of a reaction is:
options: the minimum extra energy that reactant molecules must acquire to form products
the energy released when products form
the same as the enthalpy of reaction
the total energy of the products
questions.explanation: It is the energy barrier between reactants and the activated complex.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The overall order of the reaction with rate law rate = k[NO]²[O₂] is:
questions.explanation: The overall order is the sum of the powers: 2 + 1 = 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the unit of the rate constant for a second-order reaction?
questions.explanation: k = rate/[A]² = (mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹)/(mol L⁻¹)² = L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The rate of a reaction doubles for every 10 K rise in temperature. By what factor does the rate increase when the temperature is raised from 300 K to 330 K?
questions.explanation: A 30 K rise corresponds to three 10 K steps, so the factor is 2³ = 8.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reaction proceeds in two steps: (1) A + B → C (slow) and (2) C + A → D (fast). The rate law for the overall reaction is:
questions.explanation: The rate is controlled by the slow step, which involves one A and one B.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the rate-determining step of a reaction?
questions.answer: In a multistep reaction, the slowest step is the rate-determining step. The overall rate of the reaction is controlled by it, and the rate law is written from its molecularity.
keyPoints: It is the slowest step of the mechanism
Rate law follows the reactants of this step
questions.explanation: Faster steps do not influence the overall rate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The half-life of a first-order reaction is 20 minutes. What fraction of the reactant remains after 1 hour?
questions.answer: 1 hour = 60 min = 3 half-lives, so the fraction remaining is (1/2)³ = 1/8 (12.5%).
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction each half-life halves the concentration.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Activated charcoal is used in gas masks because it:
options: reacts chemically with all gases to form salts
dissolves poisonous gases in its bulk
adsorbs poisonous gases on its very large surface area
questions.explanation: Activated charcoal has a highly porous structure with a large surface area that adsorbs toxic gases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Fog is a colloidal system in which:
options: a solid is dispersed in a gas
a liquid is dispersed in a gas
a gas is dispersed in a liquid
a gas is dispersed in a solid
questions.explanation: Fog consists of tiny liquid droplets suspended in air (a liquid aerosol).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Colloidal particles of the ferric hydroxide sol carry:
options: a charge that is positive or negative depending on particle size
questions.explanation: Fe(OH)₃ sol particles adsorb Fe³⁺ ions and are positively charged; As₂S₃ sol is negatively charged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Peptization is the process of:
options: converting a freshly prepared precipitate into a colloidal sol by adding a small amount of a suitable electrolyte
coagulating a sol by adding excess electrolyte
removing dissolved ions from a sol by a membrane
adsorbing a gas on a solid
questions.explanation: The added electrolyte provides ions that are adsorbed on the precipitate particles, breaking them into colloidal size.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The enzyme urease catalyses only the hydrolysis of urea and not of other amides. This illustrates which feature of enzyme catalysis?
options: Need for a large amount of enzyme
questions.explanation: Each enzyme has an active site that fits one particular substrate, so it acts on a specific reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A lyophilic sol used as a protective colloid is more effective when its gold number is:
questions.explanation: Gold number is the minimum mass (mg) of protective colloid that prevents coagulation of a standard gold sol; the smaller the value, the greater the protective power.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is dialysis? Give one application.
questions.answer: Dialysis is the separation of a colloid from dissolved ions or molecules by passing the mixture through a parchment or cellophane membrane; ions pass through but colloidal particles do not. It is used in the artificial kidney (haemodialysis) to remove waste from blood.
keyPoints: Purification of a sol using a semipermeable membrane
Small ions pass, colloidal particles are retained
questions.explanation: Colloidal particles are too large to cross the membrane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why are deltas formed at the places where rivers meet the sea?
questions.answer: River water carries negatively charged colloidal clay particles. Sea water contains electrolytes whose positive ions neutralise this charge and coagulate the clay, which settles to form a delta.
keyPoints: River water contains colloidal clay particles
Sea water electrolytes neutralise their charge
Coagulation and deposition form the delta
questions.explanation: This is an application of coagulation of a colloid by electrolytes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which element of group 15 exists in the white and red allotropic forms?
questions.explanation: White phosphorus is highly reactive and red phosphorus is less reactive; they are well-known allotropes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The formula of ozone is:
questions.explanation: Ozone is a triatomic allotrope of oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of the ClF₃ molecule?
questions.explanation: Chlorine has three bond pairs and two lone pairs (sp³d), giving a T-shape.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: When SO₂ is passed through an acidified KMnO₄ solution, the purple colour disappears because SO₂ acts as:
questions.explanation: SO₂ reduces purple MnO₄⁻ to nearly colourless Mn²⁺, being oxidised to sulphate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of sulphur in peroxodisulphuric acid, H₂S₂O₈ (which contains one O–O peroxide link)?
questions.explanation: Six oxygens are −2 and two are −1 (peroxide): 2(+1) + 2x + 6(−2) + 2(−1) = 0 gives x = +6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Complete hydrolysis of XeF₆ gives:
questions.explanation: XeF₆ + 3H₂O → XeO₃ + 6HF.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of copper with hot concentrated sulphuric acid.
keyPoints: Concentrated H₂SO₄ is reduced to SO₂
questions.explanation: Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as an oxidising agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The first ionisation enthalpy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen. Explain.
questions.answer: Nitrogen has the half-filled, extra-stable 2p³ configuration, so removing an electron needs more energy. In oxygen (2p⁴) the removal of one electron from a paired orbital relieves electron–electron repulsion and gives the stable half-filled p³ ion, so less energy is needed.
keyPoints: O loses a paired electron and relieves repulsion
questions.explanation: The same trend is seen across the p-block when electrons begin to pair.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which d-block metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury has a very low melting point (about 234 K).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Misch metal, used in making lighter flints, is an alloy of lanthanoid metals with a small amount of:
questions.explanation: Misch metal consists mainly of lanthanoids with some iron and traces of S, C, Ca and Al.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The paramagnetism of transition metal ions is due to:
options: the presence of only paired electrons
questions.explanation: Unpaired electrons give a net magnetic moment, which makes the ion paramagnetic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cuprous (Cu⁺) compounds are generally colourless because Cu⁺ has the configuration:
questions.explanation: Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰, so there is no vacancy in the d subshell and no d–d transition.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of Cr³⁺ (Z = 24) is:
questions.explanation: Cr³⁺ is 3d³ with 3 unpaired electrons: μ = √(3 x 5) = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An orange solution of potassium dichromate turns yellow when sodium hydroxide is added because:
options: dichromate ions are converted to chromate ions with no change in oxidation state
questions.explanation: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 2OH⁻ ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻ + H₂O; chromium stays in the +6 state.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Outline the preparation of potassium permanganate from pyrolusite (MnO₂).
questions.answer: MnO₂ is fused with KOH in the presence of air or an oxidising agent to give green K₂MnO₄ (2MnO₂ + 4KOH + O₂ → 2K₂MnO₄ + 2H₂O). The manganate is oxidised or made to disproportionate in acid solution to give purple permanganate (3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O).
keyPoints: Fusion of MnO₂ with KOH and an oxidant gives K₂MnO₄
Acidification or oxidation gives purple KMnO₄
questions.explanation: Manganese goes from +4 to +6 and then to +7.

questions.subject: chemistry
