questions.q: Write the ionic equation for the reaction of acidified dichromate with Fe²⁺ ions. How many moles of Fe²⁺ are oxidised by one mole of dichromate?
questions.answer: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O. One mole of dichromate oxidises 6 moles of Fe²⁺.
keyPoints: Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to Cr³⁺ (6 electrons gained)
questions.explanation: Each Cr changes from +6 to +3, so two Cr atoms accept 6 electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A ligand with two different donor atoms, either of which may bind to the metal, is called:
questions.explanation: Ambidentate ligands such as NO₂⁻ (N or O) and SCN⁻ (S or N) can attach through either donor atom.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The central metal ion in haemoglobin is:
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin contains iron in a porphyrin complex; chlorophyll has magnesium.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in the high-spin complex [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺?
questions.explanation: H₂O is a weak-field ligand, so Fe²⁺ (d⁶) keeps t₂g⁴e_g² with 4 unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The formula of potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II) is:
questions.explanation: The complex ion [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻ needs two K⁺ ions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following does not show geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: All six ligands are identical, so only one arrangement exists.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The crystal field stabilisation energy (CFSE) of a high-spin d⁴ ion in an octahedral field is:
questions.explanation: t₂g³e_g¹ gives 3(−0.4Δ₀) + 1(+0.6Δ₀) = −0.6Δ₀.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Mention two applications of coordination compounds.
questions.answer: Examples: EDTA is used to estimate and remove Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ (water hardness); extraction of silver and gold by cyanide complexes; purification of nickel through [Ni(CO)₄]; cisplatin is an anticancer drug.
keyPoints: Such as hardness determination with EDTA
Metal extraction or the drug cisplatin
questions.explanation: Complex formation is used in analysis, metallurgy and medicine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic while [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic.
questions.answer: Co³⁺ is d⁶. F⁻ is a weak-field ligand, so electrons do not pair (t₂g⁴e_g², four unpaired electrons, sp³d² hybridisation), making [CoF₆]³⁻ paramagnetic. NH₃ is a stronger-field ligand, so all six electrons pair in t₂g (d²sp³), making [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ diamagnetic.
keyPoints: F⁻ weak field: high spin, 4 unpaired electrons
NH₃ stronger field: low spin, no unpaired electrons
questions.explanation: Ligand field strength decides whether pairing occurs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary alkyl halide?
questions.explanation: In (CH₃)₂CHCl the carbon bearing chlorine is attached to two other carbons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The formula of iodoform is:
questions.explanation: Iodoform is triiodomethane, a yellow solid used as an antiseptic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent converts ethanol to chloroethane with only gaseous by-products (SO₂ and HCl)?
questions.explanation: Thionyl chloride gives pure alkyl chloride because both by-products escape as gases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Nitration of chlorobenzene gives mainly:
questions.explanation: Chlorine is deactivating but ortho–para directing in electrophilic substitution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of these reacts fastest by the S_N1 mechanism?
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride forms the resonance-stabilised benzyl carbocation; chlorobenzene and vinyl chloride have strong C–Cl bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many stereoisomers does 2,3-dichlorobutane have?
questions.explanation: It has two identical chiral centres, so there are two enantiomers (d and l) and one meso form.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Markovnikov's rule and give the product of the addition of HBr to propene.
questions.answer: When an unsymmetrical reagent HX adds to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen attaches to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms and the halogen to the carbon with fewer. Propene + HBr gives 2-bromopropane as the major product.
keyPoints: H goes to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms
Halogen goes to the carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms
questions.explanation: The rule follows from the more stable carbocation intermediate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Haloalkanes are polar molecules, yet they are only slightly soluble in water. Explain.
questions.answer: To dissolve, haloalkane molecules must break the strong hydrogen bonds between water molecules. The new attractions between haloalkane and water molecules are weaker than the hydrogen bonds broken, so the process is not energetically favourable.
keyPoints: Water molecules are held by hydrogen bonds
Haloalkane–water attractions are weaker than water–water hydrogen bonds
Hence little energy gain and low solubility
questions.explanation: Solubility depends on the energy balance of breaking and forming interactions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Glycerol is a:
questions.explanation: Glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) has three –OH groups.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an ether?
questions.explanation: An ether contains an oxygen atom bonded to two alkyl groups; CH₃OCH₃ is methoxymethane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to liberate:
questions.explanation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distillation of phenol with zinc dust gives:
questions.explanation: Zinc removes the oxygen of the –OH group, converting phenol to benzene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: CH₃MgBr reacts with ethanal, and the product is hydrolysed with dilute acid. The final product is:
questions.explanation: The methyl group adds to the carbonyl carbon of ethanal, giving a secondary alcohol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethyl methyl ether reacts with one equivalent of HI. The main products are:
questions.explanation: The iodide attacks the smaller, less hindered methyl group by S_N2, giving CH₃I and C₂H₅OH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How is picric acid prepared from phenol?
questions.answer: Phenol is treated with concentrated nitric acid (in presence of concentrated sulphuric acid), which nitrates the ring at the 2, 4 and 6 positions to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).
questions.explanation: The –OH group activates the ring toward electrophilic substitution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among isomeric alcohols, the boiling point decreases with increase in branching. Explain.
questions.answer: Branching makes the molecule more compact, which reduces the surface area and therefore the van der Waals forces between molecules. Less energy is needed to separate them, so the boiling point is lower (e.g. tert-butyl alcohol boils lower than butan-1-ol).
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding is present in all isomers; the difference comes from van der Waals forces.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Formalin is a solution of about 40% of which compound in water?
questions.explanation: Formalin is an aqueous solution of methanal (formaldehyde), used to preserve biological specimens.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Vinegar is a dilute aqueous solution of:
questions.explanation: Vinegar contains about 5–8% ethanoic (acetic) acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The characteristic reaction of the carbonyl group in aldehydes and ketones is:
questions.explanation: The carbonyl carbon is electron-deficient and is attacked by nucleophiles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Propan-2-ol is oxidised with K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄. The product is:
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent can distinguish benzoic acid from phenol?
questions.explanation: Benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence of CO₂ with NaHCO₃; phenol is too weak an acid to do so.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanoic acid is reduced with LiAlH₄ and then treated with water. The product is:
questions.explanation: LiAlH₄ reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write two uses of methanal.
questions.answer: Methanal (as formalin, 40% solution) is used to preserve biological specimens, and in making Bakelite and other polymers (urea–formaldehyde resins).
keyPoints: Manufacture of Bakelite and other resins
questions.explanation: Both uses are standard textbook applications.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than aldehydes, ketones and alcohols of comparable molecular masses?
questions.answer: Carboxylic acid molecules form stable hydrogen-bonded dimers through their –COOH groups (two H-bonds per pair), and this extensive association needs much more energy to break than the dipole–dipole forces in aldehydes and ketones or the single hydrogen bonds in alcohols.
keyPoints: Stronger than forces in aldehydes, ketones or alcohols
questions.explanation: Stronger intermolecular attraction gives a higher boiling point.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂NH₂ is:
questions.explanation: A two-carbon chain with –NH₂ is ethanamine (ethylamine).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On standing in air, pure aniline gradually turns:
questions.explanation: Aniline is colourless when freshly distilled but darkens because it is oxidised by air.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reduction of ethanenitrile (CH₃CN) with LiAlH₄ gives:
questions.explanation: Nitriles are reduced to primary amines containing the same number of carbons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Heating an alkyl halide with an alcoholic solution of ammonia gives:
options: a mixture of primary, secondary and tertiary amines and a quaternary salt
questions.explanation: The amine formed is itself nucleophilic and reacts further with the alkyl halide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the gas phase, the order of basic strength of methyl-substituted amines is:
questions.explanation: Without solvation effects, each added alkyl group's +I effect increases basicity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol in alkaline medium to give:
questions.explanation: Coupling at the para position of phenoxide gives an azo dye.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the carbylamine reaction? Write the equation for ethylamine.
questions.answer: Primary amines on heating with chloroform and alcoholic KOH form foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamines). C₂H₅NH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH → C₂H₅NC + 3KCl + 3H₂O. It is a test for primary amines.
questions.explanation: Secondary and tertiary amines do not give this test.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Lower aliphatic amines are soluble in water but aniline is only slightly soluble. Explain.
questions.answer: Lower aliphatic amines form hydrogen bonds with water through the N–H and lone pair. In aniline the large hydrophobic benzene ring outweighs the hydrogen-bonding –NH₂ group, so solubility is low. Solubility of aliphatic amines also falls as the alkyl part grows.
keyPoints: Lower amines hydrogen bond with water
Large hydrocarbon part of aniline is hydrophobic
Solubility decreases as the hydrocarbon part increases
questions.explanation: Solubility reflects the balance of polar and non-polar parts.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which monosaccharide is the sweetest of all sugars?
questions.explanation: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar and is found in honey and fruits.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cellulose is a polymer of:
questions.explanation: Cellulose has β-glycosidic linkages between β-D-glucose units.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Insulin, which helps regulate blood glucose, is:
questions.explanation: Insulin is a small protein (polypeptide) hormone.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The α-helix of a protein is an example of its:
questions.explanation: α-Helix and β-pleated sheet are secondary structures stabilised by hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A nucleotide is composed of:
options: a nitrogenous base and a sugar only
a phosphate group and a sugar only
an amino acid and a sugar
a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate group
questions.explanation: A nucleoside is base + sugar; adding a phosphate group gives the nucleotide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which vitamin contains cobalt?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B₁₂ (cyanocobalamin) has a cobalt ion at its centre.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is a glycosidic linkage?
questions.answer: A glycosidic linkage is the oxide (–O–) bridge that joins two monosaccharide units through the loss of a water molecule between their hydroxyl groups, as in sucrose, maltose and lactose.
keyPoints: C–O–C bridge between two monosaccharide units
questions.explanation: It is the bond that links sugar units into larger carbohydrates.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why can humans digest starch but not cellulose?
questions.answer: Starch has α-glycosidic linkages, which human digestive enzymes (amylase) can hydrolyse. Cellulose has β-glycosidic linkages, and humans lack the enzyme cellulase needed to break them.
keyPoints: Starch has α-glycosidic links, cellulose has β-links
questions.explanation: Enzymes are specific to the type of linkage.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a covalent (network) solid?
questions.explanation: In diamond every carbon atom is joined to four others by covalent bonds throughout the crystal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The smallest repeating portion of a crystal lattice, which generates the whole lattice when repeated in three dimensions, is called the:
questions.explanation: A unit cell is the smallest repeating unit of the lattice.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of an atom in a simple cubic lattice?
questions.explanation: Each atom touches one neighbour along each of the six directions ±x, ±y, ±z.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Iron(II) oxide is usually found as Fe₀.₉₅O. This is because:
options: it contains excess iron atoms in interstitial sites
oxide ions are missing and electrons occupy the vacancies
some Fe²⁺ ions are missing and the charge is balanced by some Fe³⁺ ions
some Fe²⁺ ions have moved to interstitial sites
questions.explanation: Metal-deficiency defect: loss of Fe²⁺ is compensated by oxidation of other Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Atoms of X form a ccp lattice and atoms of Y occupy all the tetrahedral voids. The formula of the compound is:
questions.explanation: For N atoms of X there are 2N tetrahedral voids, all filled by Y, giving X : Y = 1 : 2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Sodium crystallises in a bcc lattice with edge length 429 pm. Taking the molar mass as 23 g/mol and N_A = 6.022 x 10²³, its density is about:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define the term 'unit cell'.
questions.answer: A unit cell is the smallest portion of a crystal lattice which, when repeated in all three dimensions, generates the entire lattice.
keyPoints: Smallest repeating unit of the crystal lattice
Repetition in three dimensions builds the crystal
questions.explanation: Unit cells are described by edge lengths and the angles between the edges.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How does doping silicon with a group 13 element such as boron produce a p-type semiconductor?
questions.answer: Boron has three valence electrons, so each boron atom in the silicon lattice leaves one bond short of an electron, creating an electron hole. Holes move under an electric field and carry the current, so the semiconductor is called p-type (positive hole).
keyPoints: Boron has one electron fewer than silicon
Conduction is by movement of positive holes
questions.explanation: Group 13 dopants give p-type; group 15 dopants give n-type.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which concentration term does not change with temperature?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction depends only on the amounts of components, not on volume, so it is temperature independent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Soda water is an example of a solution of:
questions.explanation: Soda water is carbon dioxide dissolved in water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the unit of the molal elevation constant K_b?
questions.explanation: From ΔT_b = K_b m, K_b = ΔT_b/m, with unit K/(mol kg⁻¹) = K kg mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A solution contains 1 mol of a non-volatile solute and 9 mol of solvent. The relative lowering of vapour pressure is:
questions.explanation: Relative lowering = mole fraction of solute = 1/(1 + 9) = 0.1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 3.0 g of a non-electrolyte is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution, which shows an osmotic pressure of 0.0821 atm at 300 K. Taking R = 0.0821 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the molar mass of the solute is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which 0.01 m aqueous solution freezes at the lowest temperature, assuming complete dissociation of the electrolytes?
questions.explanation: Al₂(SO₄)₃ gives 5 ions (i = 5), the most particles, so it has the largest depression in freezing point.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define molarity and write its unit.
questions.answer: Molarity is the number of moles of solute dissolved per litre of solution. Its unit is mol L⁻¹ (M).
keyPoints: Moles of solute per litre of solution
questions.explanation: Molarity changes with temperature because volume changes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molarity of a solution containing 4 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) in 250 mL of solution.
questions.answer: Moles of NaOH = 4/40 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 0.25 L. Molarity = 0.1/0.25 = 0.4 M.
questions.explanation: Molarity = moles/volume in litres.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In an electrolytic cell the cathode carries which charge?
questions.explanation: In an electrolytic cell the cathode is connected to the negative terminal of the source and attracts cations.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Conduction of electricity through an electrolytic solution is due to the movement of:
questions.explanation: Electrolytic conduction involves the migration of cations and anions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to Faraday's first law, the mass of a substance deposited at an electrode is directly proportional to:
options: the voltage of the source only
questions.explanation: m = Z x Q, where Q is the charge in coulombs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Given E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V and E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, the standard EMF of the cell Cu | Cu²⁺ || Ag⁺ | Ag is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the EMF at 298 K of the concentration cell Cu | Cu²⁺(0.01 M) || Cu²⁺(1.0 M) | Cu? (Use 2.303RT/F = 0.0592 V)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Limiting molar conductivities (S cm² mol⁻¹): HCl 426.2, NaCl 126.5, CH₃COONa 91.0. The limiting molar conductivity of CH₃COOH is:
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law: Λ°(CH₃COOH) = 426.2 + 91.0 − 126.5 = 390.7 S cm² mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Faraday's first law of electrolysis.
questions.answer: The amount of substance deposited or liberated at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte.
keyPoints: Mass deposited is proportional to the charge passed
questions.explanation: The proportionality constant Z is the electrochemical equivalent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does a dry cell become dead after a long time even if it has not been used?
questions.answer: The electrolyte NH₄Cl is acidic and slowly attacks the zinc container, so the zinc casing corrodes and the cell deteriorates even when not in use.
questions.explanation: The side reaction between zinc and the acidic paste continues on the shelf.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to collision theory, a collision produces products only if the colliding molecules have:
options: energy equal to or above the threshold energy and proper orientation
any energy but a head-on orientation
questions.explanation: Both sufficient energy and correct orientation are needed for an effective collision.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The order of a reaction is determined:
options: from the coefficients in the balanced equation
from the molecularity of the overall reaction
questions.explanation: Order is an experimental quantity and need not equal the stoichiometric coefficients.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: If the initial concentration of the reactant in a first-order reaction is doubled, its half-life:
questions.explanation: For first order t½ = 0.693/k, which does not involve the concentration.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For a first-order reaction, a plot of ln[A] against time is a straight line with slope:
questions.explanation: ln[A] = ln[A]₀ − kt.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In a reaction, doubling [A] with [B] constant makes the rate four times, and doubling [B] with [A] constant doubles the rate. The rate law is:
questions.explanation: The rate is proportional to [A]² and [B]¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For a first-order reaction, the time required for 99% completion is how many times the time required for 90% completion?
questions.explanation: t₉₀ = (2.303/k) log 10 and t₉₉ = (2.303/k) log 100, so the ratio is 2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define the rate of a chemical reaction.
questions.answer: The rate of a reaction is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time. It is usually expressed in mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.
keyPoints: Change in concentration per unit time
Decrease of reactant or increase of product
questions.explanation: Rate = −Δ[R]/Δt = +Δ[P]/Δt.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A plot of ln k against 1/T for a reaction is a straight line with slope −5000 K. Calculate the activation energy (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).
questions.answer: Slope = −E_a/R, so E_a = 5000 x 8.314 = 41 570 J/mol ≈ 41.6 kJ/mol.
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation gives ln k = ln A − E_a/RT.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Finely divided nickel is used as a catalyst in the:
questions.explanation: Vegetable oils are hydrogenated into fats (vanaspati) using nickel.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An emulsifying agent is added to an emulsion in order to:
options: increase the size of the droplets
questions.explanation: An emulsifier forms a protective film around droplets and prevents them from merging.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Soap molecules form micelles in water:
options: above the critical micelle concentration (and above the Kraft temperature)
questions.explanation: Above the critical micelle concentration soap anions aggregate with their hydrocarbon tails inside.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a multimolecular colloid?
questions.explanation: Sulphur sol consists of aggregates of many S₈ molecules; starch and proteins are macromolecular colloids and soap forms associated colloids.

crossCheck.note: Reviewed: kept; the key is right.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The Langmuir adsorption isotherm is based on the assumption that:
options: adsorption takes place in many layers
adsorption is limited to a monolayer on the surface
adsorbed molecules strongly attract each other
questions.explanation: Langmuir assumed a uniform surface with a single layer of adsorbed molecules.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: With a rise in temperature, the extent of chemisorption generally:
questions.explanation: Chemisorption needs activation energy, so it rises at first, but being exothermic it falls at high temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is a catalyst?
questions.answer: A catalyst is a substance that alters the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change, and is recovered unchanged at the end.
keyPoints: Changes the rate of the reaction
Remains chemically unchanged at the end
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a different path with lower activation energy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State the Hardy–Schulze rule.
questions.answer: The coagulating power of an electrolyte increases with the charge on the ion that has charge opposite to the colloidal particles. For a negative sol the order is Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺.
keyPoints: Higher charge on the oppositely charged ion gives greater coagulating power
Example order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺ for a negative sol
questions.explanation: Greater charge neutralises the colloidal charge more effectively.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Laughing gas is:
questions.explanation: Dinitrogen oxide (nitrous oxide) is called laughing gas.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which noble gas is the most abundant in dry air?
questions.explanation: Argon makes up about 0.93% of air by volume.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which hydrogen halide has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: HF molecules are associated through hydrogen bonds, raising its boiling point above those of HCl, HBr and HI.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of chlorine in HClO₄?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute sodium hydroxide to form:
questions.explanation: Cl₂ + 2NaOH (cold, dilute) → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O; with hot concentrated NaOH, chlorate forms instead.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among the hydrides of group 15, the one with the lowest boiling point is:
questions.explanation: Boiling points rise from PH₃ to SbH₃, but NH₃ is anomalously high because of hydrogen bonding, so PH₃ is lowest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Name two allotropic forms of sulphur.
questions.explanation: Both consist of S₈ rings but differ in crystal structure; rhombic is the stable form at room temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The bond dissociation enthalpy of F₂ is lower than that of Cl₂. Give the reason.
questions.answer: Fluorine atoms are very small, so the lone pairs on the two atoms in F₂ repel each other strongly. This repulsion weakens the F–F bond and lowers its bond dissociation enthalpy.
questions.explanation: The order of bond enthalpy is Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the actinoid series the electrons are progressively filled into the:
questions.explanation: Actinoids (Z = 90–103) are 5f-block elements.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The general outer electronic configuration of d-block elements is:
questions.explanation: d-Block elements are filling the (n−1)d orbitals, with one or two electrons in the outer s orbital.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The most stable oxidation state of scandium is:
questions.explanation: Loss of 3d¹4s² electrons gives Sc³⁺, which has the noble gas configuration.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Potassium dichromate is prepared industrially from the ore:
questions.explanation: Chromite ore is fused with sodium carbonate in air, and the sodium chromate formed is converted to dichromate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which lanthanoid commonly shows the +4 oxidation state in addition to +3?
questions.explanation: Ce⁴⁺ has the empty 4f⁰ configuration; Eu prefers +2 (4f⁷).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Zirconium and hafnium have almost identical atomic radii mainly because of:
questions.explanation: The poor shielding by 4f electrons shrinks Hf so that its size matches that of Zr, making them very hard to separate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are lanthanoids? Write their general electronic configuration.
questions.answer: Lanthanoids are the 14 elements following lanthanum (Z = 58–71) in which the 4f subshell is progressively filled. General configuration: [Xe] 4f¹⁻¹⁴ 5d⁰⁻¹ 6s².
questions.explanation: They are also called rare-earth elements.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do transition metals readily form alloys?
questions.answer: Transition metals have similar atomic radii, so atoms of one metal can easily replace atoms of another in the crystal lattice, forming solid solutions called alloys (e.g. brass, steel).
keyPoints: One metal's atoms replace another's in the lattice
questions.explanation: Similar sizes allow substitution without distorting the lattice much.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The number of donor atoms of the ligands attached directly to the central metal atom or ion is called its:
questions.explanation: This is the definition of coordination number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In IUPAC names of complexes, NH₃ as a ligand is named:
questions.explanation: Neutral NH₃ is called 'ammine' in complex names.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The formula of sodium hexanitrito-N-cobaltate(III) is:
questions.explanation: Co³⁺ + 6 NO₂⁻ gives a 3− complex ion, needing three Na⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of compounds shows linkage isomerism?
questions.explanation: The ambidentate NO₂⁻ ligand is bonded through N in one and through O in the other.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are the coordination number and oxidation state of chromium in K₃[Cr(C₂O₄)₃]? (oxalate is bidentate)
questions.explanation: Three bidentate oxalates give coordination number 6; 3(+1) + x + 3(−2) = 0 gives x = +3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: [Ni(CO)₄] has which hybridisation and shape?
questions.explanation: Ni(0) is effectively d¹⁰; four CO ligands use the 4s and three 4p orbitals, so it is sp³ and tetrahedral (diamagnetic).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is a chelate? Give one example.
questions.answer: A chelate is a complex in which a polydentate (di- or polydentate) ligand binds to the central metal through two or more donor atoms, forming ring structures. Example: [Co(en)₃]³⁺ or the EDTA complex of Ca²⁺.
keyPoints: Polydentate ligand binds through more than one donor atom
questions.explanation: Chelates are more stable than complexes of similar monodentate ligands.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Give two limitations of valence bond theory for coordination compounds.
questions.answer: It does not explain the colours of coordination compounds and cannot give a quantitative interpretation of their magnetic data or of thermodynamic and kinetic stabilities; it also does not explain why some complexes are inner-orbital while others are outer-orbital.
keyPoints: Does not explain colour of complexes
No quantitative treatment of magnetic or stability data
questions.explanation: Crystal field theory overcomes these limitations.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Chloroform is stored in dark-coloured bottles to prevent its:
options: oxidation by air to poisonous phosgene
questions.explanation: In light and air, chloroform is slowly oxidised to carbonyl chloride (phosgene), which is toxic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The compound CCl₂F₂ is commonly known as:
questions.explanation: CCl₂F₂ is the chlorofluorocarbon known as Freon-12.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which compound has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: For the same alkyl group, boiling point increases with the size and polarisability of the halogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of methane with chlorine in sunlight proceeds by:
questions.explanation: UV light splits Cl₂ into chlorine radicals, starting a radical chain substitution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Chlorobenzene heated with aqueous NaOH at about 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification, gives:
questions.explanation: Under these drastic conditions the –Cl is replaced by –OH (Dow process), giving phenol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: DDT, an insecticide, is chemically:
questions.explanation: DDT stands for dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane; it is a persistent organochlorine compound.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the IUPAC name of CH₃CHClCH₂CH₃.
questions.explanation: Number the chain from the end that gives the halogen the lowest locant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the Swarts reaction? Give an example.
questions.answer: Alkyl chlorides or bromides are heated with a metallic fluoride such as AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂ or SbF₃ to give alkyl fluorides, e.g. CH₃Br + AgF → CH₃F + AgBr.
keyPoints: Reagent: AgF, Hg₂F₂, CoF₂ or SbF₃
Example such as CH₃Br + AgF → CH₃F + AgBr
questions.explanation: Direct fluorination is too violent, so halogen exchange is used.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: A three-carbon chain with –OH on the end carbon is propan-1-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol is oxidised by an excess of acidified potassium dichromate to:
questions.explanation: A primary alcohol is oxidised first to the aldehyde and then to the carboxylic acid by strong oxidising agents.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Diethyl ether is obtained by heating excess ethanol with concentrated H₂SO₄ at about:
questions.explanation: At about 413 K the intermolecular dehydration gives ether; at 443 K ethene is formed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Phenol dissolves in aqueous NaOH but not in aqueous NaHCO₃ because:
options: phenol is a weaker acid than carbonic acid
NaHCO₃ is a stronger base than NaOH
questions.explanation: Phenol is acidic enough to react with a strong base but not with the weak base HCO₃⁻.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which alcohol resists oxidation by mild oxidising agents because it has no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the –OH group?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols lack an α-hydrogen, so they are not oxidised without breaking C–C bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Sodium phenoxide is heated with CO₂ at about 400 K and 4–7 atm, and then acidified. The product is:
questions.explanation: This is the Kolbe reaction, which introduces –COOH at the ortho position of phenol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is absolute alcohol and how is it obtained from rectified spirit?
questions.answer: Absolute alcohol is practically 100% pure ethanol. It is obtained from rectified spirit (95% ethanol) by azeotropic distillation with benzene, which removes the water.
keyPoints: Rectified spirit is a 95% azeotrope with water
Water is removed by distillation with benzene
questions.explanation: Ordinary distillation cannot remove the last 5% water because of the azeotrope.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is ethanol completely miscible with water while hexan-1-ol is only slightly soluble?
questions.answer: Both form hydrogen bonds with water through –OH, but in hexan-1-ol the large non-polar hydrocarbon chain disrupts the hydrogen bonding of water and outweighs the polar group. Ethanol's short chain has a small non-polar part, so solubility is high.
keyPoints: Solubility falls as the alkyl chain grows
questions.explanation: Solubility reflects the balance of polar and non-polar parts.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which acid is responsible for the pain of an ant sting?
questions.explanation: Methanoic (formic) acid occurs in red ants, hence its name.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a ketone?
questions.explanation: CH₃COCH₂CH₃ (butanone) has a carbonyl group between two carbon atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reduction of the C=O group to CH₂ using hydrazine and KOH in ethylene glycol is called:
questions.explanation: Wolff–Kishner reduction uses NH₂NH₂/KOH at high temperature in a basic medium.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanal reacts with HCN to give:
questions.explanation: HCN adds across the C=O bond: CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzoic acid is treated with Cl₂ in the presence of FeCl₃. The main product is:
options: a mixture of ortho and para isomers
questions.explanation: The –COOH group deactivates the ring and directs the incoming electrophile to the meta position.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A compound of formula C₃H₆O reduces Tollens' reagent. It must be:
questions.explanation: Only an aldehyde gives a silver mirror; propanal is the aldehyde with formula C₃H₆O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the functional group and the general formula of a carboxylic acid.
questions.answer: The functional group is the carboxyl group, –COOH. For saturated monocarboxylic acids the general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (or R–COOH).
questions.explanation: The carboxyl group combines a carbonyl and a hydroxyl group.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How is benzoic acid prepared from toluene?
questions.answer: Toluene is oxidised by heating with alkaline KMnO₄ (or acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇); the side-chain –CH₃ is oxidised to –COOH, and acidification liberates benzoic acid.
keyPoints: Oxidation of the side chain of toluene
Reagent: alkaline or acidic KMnO₄ (or K₂Cr₂O₇)
questions.explanation: Any alkyl side chain with a benzylic hydrogen is oxidised to –COOH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many alkyl groups are attached to the nitrogen atom in a tertiary amine?
questions.explanation: In a tertiary amine all three hydrogens of NH₃ are replaced by alkyl or aryl groups.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Methylamine at room temperature is a:
questions.explanation: The lowest members of the aliphatic amines, such as methylamine, are gases with a fishy smell.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aniline can be prepared from nitrobenzene by:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen over a palladium or nickel catalyst reduces the nitro group to an amino group.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aniline reacts with acetic anhydride to give:
questions.explanation: Acetylation of the –NH₂ group gives N-phenylethanamide (acetanilide).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the weakest base?
questions.explanation: The –NO₂ group withdraws electrons and further lowers the availability of the lone pair on nitrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with CuCN (Sandmeyer reaction) to give:
questions.explanation: The diazonium group is replaced by –CN, giving C₆H₅CN.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define primary, secondary and tertiary amines with one example each.
questions.answer: A primary amine has one alkyl/aryl group on nitrogen (CH₃NH₂), a secondary amine has two (CH₃NHCH₃) and a tertiary amine has three ((CH₃)₃N).
questions.explanation: Classification depends on the number of hydrogens of NH₃ replaced.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do primary amines have higher boiling points than tertiary amines of comparable molar mass?
questions.answer: Primary amines have two N–H bonds and form intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Tertiary amines have no N–H bond and so cannot form hydrogen bonds with each other, so their boiling points are lower.
keyPoints: Primary amines have N–H and hydrogen-bond with each other
Tertiary amines have no N–H bond
Hydrogen bonding raises the boiling point
questions.explanation: The order of boiling points is primary > secondary > tertiary.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.explanation: Lactose is composed of galactose and glucose units.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Vitamin K is needed for:
questions.explanation: Vitamin K helps in the synthesis of prothrombin, needed for blood clotting.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which common α-amino acid is optically inactive?
questions.explanation: In glycine the α-carbon carries two hydrogens, so it is not chiral.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Starch is hydrolysed to maltose by the enzyme:
questions.explanation: Amylase (diastase) breaks starch into maltose; maltase then gives glucose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In protein synthesis, which nucleic acid carries amino acids to the ribosome?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA (tRNA) binds specific amino acids and delivers them according to the codons of mRNA.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Complete hydrolysis of DNA gives:
options: phosphoric acid, ribose and the bases A, G, C and U
amino acids and phosphoric acid only
phosphoric acid, deoxyribose and the bases A, G, C and T
questions.explanation: DNA is made of phosphate, 2-deoxyribose and the four bases adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are enzymes?
questions.answer: Enzymes are biological catalysts, mostly globular proteins, that speed up specific biochemical reactions in living organisms without being used up.
questions.explanation: Each enzyme acts on a particular substrate.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between fibrous and globular proteins with one example of each.
questions.answer: Fibrous proteins have long thread-like polypeptide chains held together by hydrogen and disulphide bonds; they are insoluble in water (e.g. keratin, myosin). Globular proteins have chains folded into a spherical shape and are usually soluble in water (e.g. insulin, albumin).
keyPoints: Fibrous: thread-like, insoluble in water, e.g. keratin
Globular: spherical, soluble in water, e.g. insulin or albumin
questions.explanation: The shape of the polypeptide chain determines the solubility and function.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many crystal systems are there?
questions.explanation: There are seven crystal systems (cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, hexagonal, rhombohedral, monoclinic, triclinic); the 14 Bravais lattices belong to them.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The stacking pattern ABABAB… of close-packed layers gives:
questions.explanation: ABAB stacking is hexagonal close packing; ABCABC stacking is cubic close packing.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In a close-packed structure of spheres of radius r, the radius of an octahedral void is:
questions.explanation: The octahedral void has radius 0.414 r and the tetrahedral void 0.225 r.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Frenkel defect is most likely to be found in crystals in which:
options: both ions have the same size
the coordination number is very high
the cation is much smaller than the anion
the anion is much smaller than the cation
questions.explanation: The small cation can move into an interstitial site, as in AgBr and ZnS.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: CsCl has one formula unit per cubic unit cell of edge 412 pm. Taking its molar mass as 168.4 g/mol and N_A = 6.022 x 10²³, its density is about:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the NaCl structure the ions touch along the cell edge. If r(Na⁺) = 95 pm and r(Cl⁻) = 181 pm, the edge length of the unit cell is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 10 g of a solute is dissolved in 90 g of solvent. The mass percentage of the solute is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Of two solutions, the one with the lower osmotic pressure is called:
questions.explanation: A hypotonic solution has lower osmotic pressure than the other; a hypertonic solution has higher.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Soft drinks are bottled under a high pressure of CO₂ in order to:
options: lower the temperature of the drink
prevent the formation of any carbonic acid
questions.explanation: By Henry's law, a higher partial pressure of CO₂ increases its solubility.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A solution contains 2 mol of solute and 8 mol of solvent. The mole fraction of the solute is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An ideal solution is made of equal moles of liquids A and B, whose pure vapour pressures at a given temperature are 100 mmHg and 60 mmHg. The total vapour pressure of the solution is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A and B form an ideal solution in equal moles; the pure vapour pressures are 100 mmHg (A) and 60 mmHg (B). The mole fraction of A in the vapour phase is:
questions.explanation: p_A = 50 mmHg and P_total = 80 mmHg, so y_A = 50/80 = 0.625.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The unit of the cell constant of a conductivity cell is:
questions.explanation: Cell constant = l/A, so its unit is length⁻¹ (cm⁻¹ or m⁻¹).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: One faraday (1 F) is the charge carried by:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Rust is chiefly:
questions.explanation: Iron corrodes in moist air to form hydrated ferric oxide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The molar conductivity of acetic acid rises much more steeply on dilution than that of KCl because, on dilution:
options: the degree of dissociation of acetic acid increases
viscosity of acetic acid decreases sharply
questions.explanation: A weak electrolyte ionises more as it is diluted, increasing the number of ions per mole.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How much time is needed for a current of 1.0 A to deposit 1.08 g of silver from AgNO₃ solution? (Ag = 108 g/mol, F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: 1.08 g = 0.01 mol Ag, which needs 0.01 F = 965 C; t = 965 C/1.0 A = 965 s.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Given E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, the EMF of the cell Zn | Zn²⁺ (1 M) || H⁺ (1 M) | H₂ (1 atm) | Pt is:

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The rate of most reactions decreases as the reaction proceeds because:
questions.explanation: Rate depends on reactant concentrations, which decrease with time.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The half-life of a reaction is the time in which the concentration of the reactant:
options: falls to half of its initial value
questions.explanation: This is the definition of half-life, t½.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Radioactive decay follows:
questions.explanation: The rate of decay is proportional to the number of radioactive nuclei present.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At a fixed temperature, lowering the activation energy of a reaction (for example by a catalyst):
options: has no effect on the rate constant
questions.explanation: k = A e^(−E_a/RT), so a smaller E_a gives a larger k.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The half-life of a first-order reaction is 30 minutes. The time needed for 87.5% of the reactant to be consumed is:
questions.explanation: 87.5% consumed leaves 12.5% = (1/2)³, i.e. 3 half-lives = 90 min.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For A → products, the initial rate is 2 x 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ at [A] = 0.1 M and 8 x 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ at [A] = 0.2 M. The rate constant is:
questions.explanation: Doubling [A] quadruples the rate, so the order is 2; k = 2 x 10⁻⁴/(0.1)² = 2 x 10⁻² L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a lyophobic sol?
questions.explanation: Metal sols are lyophobic (solvent-hating) and need stabilisers; gelatin, starch and gum are lyophilic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At constant temperature, the extent of physisorption of a gas on a solid generally:
options: decreases with an increase in pressure
increases with an increase in pressure
is independent of pressure at all pressures
falls to zero at high pressure
questions.explanation: Adsorption increases with pressure until the surface is saturated.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Mixing two oppositely charged sols leads to:
questions.explanation: The opposite charges neutralise each other, so the particles aggregate and settle.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The catalyst used in the Ostwald process for oxidising ammonia is:
questions.explanation: Platinum (with rhodium) gauze catalyses the oxidation of NH₃ to NO at about 800 °C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the Haber process, molybdenum increases the activity of the iron catalyst. Molybdenum is therefore a:
questions.explanation: A substance that enhances the activity of a catalyst is called a promoter.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Lyophobic sols are kept stable mainly by:
options: the like electric charge on the particles, which makes them repel one another
questions.explanation: Particles of a sol carry the same charge, which prevents them from coming together and coagulating.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which allotrope of phosphorus is the most reactive and glows in the dark?
questions.explanation: White phosphorus (P₄) is highly reactive and shows chemiluminescence.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Oleum is:
questions.explanation: Oleum is formed by dissolving SO₃ in concentrated H₂SO₄.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ammonia gas reacts with hydrogen chloride gas to give dense white fumes of:
questions.explanation: NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl, a white solid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ozone present in the stratosphere is important because it:
options: absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun
causes the greenhouse effect near the ground
questions.explanation: The ozone layer absorbs most of the sun's harmful UV rays.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On heating, phosphorous acid (H₃PO₃) disproportionates to give:
questions.explanation: 4H₃PO₃ → 3H₃PO₄ + PH₃; phosphorus goes from +3 to +5 and −3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The basicity (number of ionisable hydrogen atoms) of phosphorous acid, H₃PO₃, is:
questions.explanation: H₃PO₃ has two –OH groups and one P–H bond, so only two hydrogens are acidic (dibasic).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Iron is galvanised by coating it with:
questions.explanation: Zinc coating protects iron from rusting.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not a d-block element?
questions.explanation: Calcium is an s-block element.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many 3d electrons does the Fe³⁺ ion have?
questions.explanation: Fe is [Ar]3d⁶4s²; removing two 4s and one 3d electron leaves 3d⁵.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Excess aqueous ammonia is added to a solution of copper(II) sulphate. The result is:
options: a black precipitate of CuO that does not dissolve
questions.explanation: A pale blue precipitate first forms and dissolves in excess ammonia to give the deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In neutral or weakly alkaline solution, KMnO₄ is reduced to:
questions.explanation: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻ in neutral or weakly alkaline medium.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of Fe²⁺ (high spin, 3d⁶) is:
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ has 4 unpaired electrons: μ = √(4 x 6) = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a neutral ligand?
questions.explanation: H₂O carries no charge; the others are anions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cisplatin, a drug used in cancer treatment, is a coordination compound of:
questions.explanation: Cisplatin is cis-[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂].

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆] and [Cr(NH₃)₆][Co(CN)₆] are examples of:
questions.explanation: The ligands are exchanged between the cationic and anionic complexes, which is coordination isomerism.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is a diamagnetic octahedral complex. Its hybridisation is:
questions.explanation: NH₃ pairs the d electrons of Co³⁺ (d⁶), leaving two 3d orbitals vacant for d²sp³ hybridisation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many ions are produced in solution when one formula unit of [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ dissolves?
questions.explanation: It gives one [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺ ion and two Cl⁻ ions, 3 in total.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following complexes is the most stable, owing to the chelate effect?
questions.explanation: A bidentate ligand such as ethane-1,2-diamine forms stable five-membered rings, increasing stability.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the formula of hexaamminecobalt(III) chloride.
questions.explanation: The complex cation has charge +3, balanced by three Cl⁻.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An alkyl bromide reacts with magnesium in dry ether to give:
questions.explanation: RBr + Mg → RMgBr in dry ether.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol reacts with PCl₅ to give chloroethane along with:
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH + PCl₅ → C₂H₅Cl + POCl₃ + HCl.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is chiral?
questions.explanation: The carbon in CHFClBr bears four different atoms (H, F, Cl, Br).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethyl bromide on heating with alcoholic KOH gives:
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH brings about dehydrohalogenation (β-elimination) to give an alkene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Hydrolysis of optically active 2-bromobutane by the S_N1 mechanism gives:
options: only the product with retention of configuration
only the product with inversion of configuration
questions.explanation: The planar carbocation can be attacked from either face with equal probability, giving equal amounts of both enantiomers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many structural isomers of C₄H₉Br exist?
questions.explanation: They are 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Name the product when benzene reacts with chlorine in the presence of anhydrous FeCl₃.
questions.answer: Chlorobenzene (by electrophilic substitution), with HCl as the by-product.
questions.explanation: FeCl₃ acts as a Lewis acid catalyst that polarises Cl₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A major use of ethane-1,2-diol is as:
questions.explanation: Ethylene glycol lowers the freezing point of water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which ether was used for a long time as an anaesthetic?
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether (ethoxyethane) was widely used as a general anaesthetic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst to give an ester is called:
questions.explanation: RCOOH + R'OH ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O is esterification.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Propene is treated with diborane (B₂H₆) and then with H₂O₂/NaOH. The product is:
questions.explanation: Hydroboration–oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov alcohol, propan-1-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which nitrophenol isomer is steam volatile?
questions.explanation: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so it does not associate and is volatile; the p-isomer is associated by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many isomeric alcohols have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O?
questions.explanation: They are butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is Lucas reagent and what is it used for?
questions.answer: Lucas reagent is a solution of anhydrous zinc chloride in concentrated hydrochloric acid. It is used to distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols by the rate at which turbidity appears.
questions.explanation: Turbidity is due to the insoluble alkyl chloride.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ketones are obtained by the oxidation of:
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones; primary alcohols give aldehydes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Pure, anhydrous ethanoic acid, which freezes to an ice-like solid at about 290 K, is called:
questions.explanation: Its ice-like crystals on cooling give the name glacial acetic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The aldol condensation product of two molecules of ethanal (before dehydration) is:
questions.explanation: 2CH₃CHO → CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO, which is 3-hydroxybutanal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzaldehyde reacts with Tollens' reagent to give:
options: benzoic acid (as benzoate) and a silver mirror
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde is oxidised to benzoate by Ag⁺ in ammonia, depositing silver.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: Alkyl groups donate electrons and reduce acidity, so methanoic acid (no alkyl group) is the strongest of these.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A Grignard reagent CH₃MgBr is treated with solid CO₂ and then hydrolysed with dilute acid. The product is:
questions.explanation: CH₃MgBr adds to CO₂ to give CH₃COOMgBr, which on hydrolysis gives CH₃COOH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CHCHO.
questions.explanation: The aldehyde carbon is numbered 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The functional group present in amines is:
questions.explanation: Amines are derivatives of ammonia, with one or more hydrogens replaced by alkyl or aryl groups.

crossCheck.note: The option wording is hedged ("–NH2 (amino group) or its substituted forms"), so the item is weakly worded; D is still the amine functional group. Reviewed: kept; the key is right.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Gabriel synthesis of primary amines starts from:
questions.explanation: Potassium phthalimide reacts with an alkyl halide, and alkaline hydrolysis releases the primary amine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: O–H···O hydrogen bonds are stronger than N–H···N bonds, and ethers and alkanes have no hydrogen bonding.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which sequence of reagents is used in the azo dye test for aromatic primary amines?
options: NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5 °C followed by alkaline β-naphthol
questions.explanation: The diazonium salt couples with β-naphthol to give an orange-red azo dye.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Aniline dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid because:
options: it is oxidised by the acid
anilinium chloride, a water-soluble salt, is formed
questions.explanation: The basic –NH₂ group is protonated, giving the ionic C₆H₅NH₃⁺Cl⁻.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many isomeric amines have the molecular formula C₃H₉N?
questions.explanation: Propan-1-amine, propan-2-amine, N-methylethanamine and N,N-dimethylmethanamine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Give the IUPAC name of aniline.
keyPoints: Aniline is the accepted common name
questions.explanation: The –NH₂ group on benzene is named as an amine.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Proteins are polymers of:
questions.explanation: Amino acids are joined by peptide bonds to form proteins.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Fats and oils are esters of glycerol with:
questions.explanation: Triglycerides contain three fatty acid chains attached to glycerol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Proteins found in living organisms are made up of about how many different α-amino acids?
questions.explanation: About 20 α-amino acids occur commonly in proteins.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The disaccharide present in milk is:
questions.explanation: Lactose, or milk sugar, is formed from galactose and glucose.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Glucose is oxidised by bromine water to:
questions.explanation: Bromine water oxidises only the aldehyde group, giving the monocarboxylic gluconic acid; this shows the presence of –CHO.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Prolonged heating of glucose with HI gives:
questions.explanation: Complete reduction to n-hexane shows that all six carbon atoms are in a straight chain.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Name the monomer units of proteins and the bond that joins them.
questions.answer: The monomers are α-amino acids, joined by peptide (amide, –CO–NH–) bonds.
questions.explanation: A peptide bond forms between –COOH and –NH₂ with loss of water.
